title.zh: 卷四百三十三 列傳第一百九十二 儒林三 邵伯溫 喻樗 洪興祖 高閌 程大昌 林之奇 林光朝 楊萬里
title.en: Volume 433 Biographies 192: Confucian Scholars 3 - Shao Bowen, Yu Chu, Hong Xingzu, Gao Kang, Cheng Dachang, Lin Zhiqi, Lin Guangchao, Yang Wanli
title.raw: 卷四百三十三 列傳第一百九十二 儒林三 邵伯溫 喻樗 洪興祖 高閌 程大昌 林之奇 林光朝 楊萬里 Volume 433 Biographies 192: Confucian Scholars 3 - Shao Bowen, Yu Chu, Hong Xingzu, Gao Kang, Cheng Dachang, Lin Zhiqi, Lin Guangchao, Yang Wanli

sentences.zh: 邵伯溫 喻樗 洪興祖 高閌 程大昌 林之奇 林光朝 楊萬里

translations.literal: Shao Bowen, Yu Chu, Hong Xingzu, Gao Kang, Cheng Dachang, Lin Zhiqi, Lin Guangchao, Yang Wanli
translations.idiomatic: Shao Bowen, Yu Chu, Hong Xingzu, Gao Kang, Cheng Dachang, Lin Zhiqi, Lin Guangchao, and Yang Wanli

sentences.zh: 邵伯溫

translations.literal: Shao Bowen
translations.idiomatic: Shao Bowen

sentences.zh: 邵伯溫，字子文，洛陽人，康節處士雍之子也。

translations.literal: Shao Bowen, courtesy name Ziwen, was a man of Luoyang, the son of the recluse Kangjie, Master Shao Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Bowen, whose courtesy name was Ziwen, came from Luoyang and was the son of Shao Yong, the Kangjie Recluse.

sentences.zh: 雍名重一時，如司馬光、韓維、呂公著、程頤兄弟皆交其門。

translations.literal: Yong's fame weighed heavily in his age; men such as Sima Guang, Han Wei, Lü Gongzhuo, and the Cheng brothers Yi and Hao all associated with his household.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's reputation stood at the height of the age, and figures such as Sima Guang, Han Wei, Lü Gongzhuo, and the Cheng brothers all sought his company.

sentences.zh: 伯溫入聞父教，出則事司馬光等，而光等亦屈名位輩行，與伯溫為再世交，故所聞日博，而尤熟當世之務。

translations.literal: At home Bowen heard his father's teaching; abroad he attended on Sima Guang and the others, while they too lowered rank and seniority to be friends with Bowen as if across two generations—thus what he heard grew daily broader, and he became especially versed in the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: At home Bowen absorbed his father's instruction; abroad he moved in the circle of Sima Guang and the rest, who in turn set aside rank and seniority to treat him as a friend across two generations. What he learned thus grew ever wider, and he became especially adept at the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 光入相，嘗欲薦伯溫，未果而薨。

translations.literal: When Guang entered the chancellorship, he once wished to recommend Bowen, but before it was accomplished he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Guang became chief minister, he had wished to recommend Bowen, but died before he could do so.

sentences.zh: 後以河南尹與部使者薦，特授大名府助教，調潞州長子縣尉。

translations.literal: Later, on recommendation from the Intendant of Henan and the circuit commissioners, he was specially appointed Assistant Instructor of Daming Prefecture and transferred to be Assistant Magistrate of Changzi County in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recommended by the Intendant of Henan and the circuit commissioners, given a special appointment as assistant instructor in Daming Prefecture, and transferred to serve as assistant magistrate of Changzi County in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，蔡確之相也，神宗崩，哲宗立，邢恕自襄州移河陽，詣確謀造定策事。

translations.literal: Early on, when Cai Que was chief minister, Emperor Shenzong died and Emperor Zhezong acceded; Xing Shu was transferred from Xiangzhou to Heyang and went to Que to plot the affair of establishing the succession policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Que was chief minister, Shenzong died and Zhezong succeeded. Xing Shu was moved from Xiangzhou to Heyang and went to Que to plot how to fix the succession in their favor.

sentences.zh: 及司馬光子康詣闕，恕召康詣河陽，伯溫謂康曰：「公休除喪未見君，不宜枉道先見朋友。」

translations.literal: When Sima Guang's son Kang went to the capital, Shu summoned Kang to Heyang. Bowen said to Kang: "You have left mourning and not yet seen the sovereign—you ought not go out of your way first to see friends."
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang's son Kang set out for the capital, Shu summoned him to Heyang. Bowen told Kang, "You have finished mourning but have not yet seen the emperor—you should not go out of your way to visit friends first."

sentences.zh: 康曰：「已諾之。」

translations.literal: Kang said: "I have already promised."
translations.idiomatic: Kang replied, "I have already given my word."

sentences.zh: 伯溫曰：「恕傾巧，或以事要公休，若從之，必為異日之悔。」

translations.literal: Bowen said: "Shu is artful and crooked; he may press you with some affair—if you comply, you will surely regret it hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: Bowen said, "Shu is devious and unscrupulous. He may try to coerce you into something. If you yield, you will regret it for years to come."

sentences.zh: 康竟往。

translations.literal: Kang went anyway.
translations.idiomatic: Kang went all the same.

sentences.zh: 恕果勸康作書稱確，以為他日全身保家計。

translations.literal: Shu indeed urged Kang to write a letter praising Que, as a plan to preserve himself and his family in days to come.
translations.idiomatic: Shu did urge Kang to write a letter commending Que, framing it as a way to protect himself and his household in the future.

sentences.zh: 康、恕同年登科，恕又出光門下，康遂作書如恕言。

translations.literal: Kang and Shu had passed the examinations in the same year; Shu had also been a student under Guang—so Kang composed the letter as Shu said.
translations.idiomatic: Kang and Shu had passed the civil examinations in the same year, and Shu had studied under Guang as well, so Kang wrote the letter as Shu wished.

sentences.zh: 恕蓋以康為光子，言確有定策功，世必見信。

translations.literal: Shu calculated that because Kang was Guang's son, if he said Que had merit in fixing the succession policy, the world would surely believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu reckoned that because Kang was Guang's son, any claim that Que had helped fix the succession would be widely credited.

sentences.zh: 既而梁燾以諫議召，恕亦要燾至河陽，連日夜論確功不休，且以康書為證，燾不悅。

translations.literal: Before long Liang Zhen was summoned as Remonstrator; Shu also wanted Zhen to come to Heyang and for days and nights talked incessantly of Que's merits, taking Kang's letter as proof—Zhen was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liang Zhen was summoned as remonstrating censor. Shu also pressed Zhen to come to Heyang and for days on end argued Que's merits without cease, citing Kang's letter as proof. Zhen was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會吳處厚奏確詩謗朝政，燾與劉安世共請誅確，且論恕罪，亦命康分折，康始悔之。

translations.literal: When Wu Chuhou memorialized Que's poetry slandering court policy, Zhen together with Liu Anshi jointly requested Que's execution and also argued for Shu's crime; Kang too was ordered to analyze the matter—only then did Kang repent.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Chuhou submitted a memorial accusing Que of seditious verse, Zhen and Liu Anshi jointly called for Que's execution and also pressed charges against Shu. Kang was ordered to examine the case as well, and only then did he repent.

sentences.zh: 康卒，子植幼。

translations.literal: Kang died; his son Zhi was young.
translations.idiomatic: Kang died, leaving his young son Zhi.

sentences.zh: 宣仁後憫之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren later took pity on them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren later showed them compassion.

sentences.zh: 呂大防謂康素以伯溫可托，請以伯溫為西京教授以教植。

translations.literal: Lü Dafang said that Kang had always regarded Bowen as one to whom affairs could be entrusted, and requested that Bowen be made Professor of the Western Capital to teach Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dafang said that Kang had always trusted Bowen with important matters and asked that Bowen be appointed professor in the Western Capital to instruct Zhi.

sentences.zh: 伯溫既至官，則誨植曰：「溫公之孫，大諫之子，賢愚在天下，可畏也。」

translations.literal: Once Bowen had taken office, he admonished Zhi: "You are Duke Wen's grandson and a Great Remonstrator's son—whether wise or foolish, it is known under Heaven and is to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: After Bowen took up his post, he exhorted Zhi: "You are the grandson of Duke Wen and the son of a great remonstrating official. Whether you prove worthy or not will be known throughout the realm—that is something to be feared."

sentences.zh: 植聞之，力學不懈，卒有立。

translations.literal: Zhi heard this, studied strenuously without slackening, and in the end achieved standing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi took this to heart, applied himself without slackening, and in the end made his mark.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，章惇為相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, Zhang Dun became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng era, Zhang Dun became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 惇嘗事康節，欲用伯溫，伯溫不往。

translations.literal: Dun had once studied under Kangjie and wished to employ Bowen, but Bowen did not go to him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun had once studied under Kangjie and wanted to employ Bowen, but Bowen would not go to him.

sentences.zh: 會法當赴吏部銓，程頤為伯溫曰：「吾危子之行也。」

translations.literal: When the law required going to the Ministry of Personnel for selection, Cheng Yi said to Bowen: "I dread your journey."
translations.idiomatic: When the regulations required him to go to the Ministry of Personnel for appointment, Cheng Yi told Bowen, "I fear for what may come of this journey."

sentences.zh: 伯溫曰：「豈不欲見先公於地下耶？」

translations.literal: Bowen said: "Would I not wish to see my late father in the grave?"
translations.idiomatic: Bowen replied, "Would I not wish to face my late father in the world below?"

sentences.zh: 至則先就部擬官，而後見宰相。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he first went to the ministry for proposed appointment, and only afterward saw the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he first went to the ministry to receive his proposed appointment and only afterward called on the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 惇論及康節之學，曰：「嗟乎，吾於先生不能卒業也。」

translations.literal: Dun spoke of Kangjie's learning and said: "Alas! I could not complete my studies with the Master."
translations.idiomatic: Dun spoke of Kangjie's learning and sighed, "Alas—I never finished my studies with the Master."

sentences.zh: 伯溫曰：「先君先天之學，論天地萬物未有不盡者。

translations.literal: Bowen said: "My late father's learning of the Prior Heaven discusses heaven, earth, and the myriad things—there is nothing he did not exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen said, "My father's teaching of the Prior Heaven encompasses heaven, earth, and the myriad things—there is nothing it does not fully treat.

sentences.zh: 其信也，則人之仇怨反覆者可忘矣。」

translations.literal: In its faithfulness, even men's enmity and reversal can be forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: In its fidelity, even the enmities and reversals of men can be set aside."

sentences.zh: 時惇方興黨獄，故以是動之。

translations.literal: At the time Dun was raising the factional prosecutions, so Bowen moved him with these words.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Dun was inflaming the factional prosecutions, and Bowen meant to stir him with these words.

sentences.zh: 惇悚然。

translations.literal: Dun was startled.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was shaken.

sentences.zh: 猶薦之於朝，而伯溫願補郡縣吏，惇不悅，遂得監永興軍鑄錢監。

translations.literal: He still recommended Bowen to the court, but Bowen wished to fill a prefectural or county post—Dun was displeased, and Bowen consequently received appointment as Superintendent of the Yongxing Army coin-casting directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He still recommended Bowen to the court, yet Bowen asked for a county or prefectural post. Dun was displeased, and Bowen was sent to superintend the Yongxing Army mint.

sentences.zh: 時元祐諸賢方南遷，士鮮訪之者。

translations.literal: At the time the worthies of the Yuanyou era were being banished south, and few scholars visited them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the worthies of the Yuanyou era were being exiled to the south, and few scholars dared visit them.

sentences.zh: 伯溫見范祖禹於咸平，見範純仁於潁昌，或為之恐，不顧也。

translations.literal: Bowen visited Fan Zuyu at Xianping and Fan Chunren at Yingchang; some were afraid for him, but he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen visited Fan Zuyu at Xianping and Fan Chunren at Yingchang. Some warned him of the danger, but he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 會西邊用兵，復夏人故地，從軍者得累數階，伯溫當行，輒推同列。

translations.literal: When war on the western border broke out and former Xia territory was recovered, those who followed the army could advance many ranks in succession—Bowen was due to go but always deferred to colleagues of the same grade.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting broke out on the western frontier and former Xia territory was recovered, those who took the field could advance several ranks in succession. Bowen was due to go but always yielded the chance to colleagues of equal rank.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，惇猶在相位。

translations.literal: When his term was up, Dun was still in the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, Dun was still chief minister.

sentences.zh: 伯溫義不至京師，從外台辟環慶路帥幕，實避惇也。

translations.literal: Bowen, on principle, would not go to the capital; he accepted appointment from the outer administration to the staff of the commander of the Huanqing circuit—in substance to avoid Dun.
translations.idiomatic: On principle Bowen would not go to the capital. He accepted an appointment from the outer administration to the staff of the Huanqing commander—a move meant in truth to avoid Dun.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，以日食求言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong acceded, he sought memorials on the occasion of a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne, he called for memorials on the occasion of a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 伯溫上書累數千言，大要欲復祖宗制度，辨宣仁誣謗，解元祐黨錮，分君子小人，戒勞民用兵，語極懇至。

translations.literal: Bowen submitted a memorial of several thousand words in all; in substance he wished to restore ancestral institutions, clear the slander against Xuanren, lift the Yuanyou faction ban, distinguish gentlemen from petty men, and warn against exhausting the people and using the army—his language was exceedingly earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen submitted a memorial of several thousand words. In substance he urged restoration of ancestral institutions, refutation of the slander against Xuanren, lifting of the Yuanyou faction ban, distinction between gentlemen and petty men, and caution against exhausting the people and resorting to war. His language was deeply earnest throughout.

sentences.zh: 宣仁太后之謗，伯溫既辨之，又著書名《辨誣》。

translations.literal: Concerning the slander against Empress Dowager Xuanren, Bowen had already argued it down and also wrote a book entitled Refutation of Slander.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen had already refuted the slander against Empress Dowager Xuanren and also wrote a book entitled Refutation of Slander.

sentences.zh: 後崇寧、大觀間，以元符上書人分邪正等，伯溫在邪等中，以此書也。

translations.literal: Later, in the Chongning and Daguan periods, those who had memorialized in the Yuanfu reign were divided into orthodox and heterodox grades—Bowen was placed among the heterodox because of this book.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during Chongning and Daguan, those who had submitted memorials in the Yuanfu era were classified as orthodox or heterodox. Bowen was placed among the heterodox on account of this book.

sentences.zh: 出監華州西嶽廟，久之，知陝州靈寶縣，徙芮城縣。

translations.literal: He was sent out to serve as Superintendent of the Western Marchmount Temple of Huazhou; after a long while he became Prefect of Lingbao County in Shanzhou, then was transferred to Ruicheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to superintend the Western Marchmount Temple in Huazhou. After a long interval he became magistrate of Lingbao County in Shanzhou and was later transferred to Ruicheng County.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，主管永興軍耀州三白渠公事。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when mourning ended he was put in charge of the Three White Canal office of Yaozhou under the Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother and completing the mourning period, he was placed in charge of the Three White Canal works at Yaozhou under the Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 童貫為宣撫使，士大夫爭出其門，伯溫聞其來，出他州避之。

translations.literal: Tong Guan served as Commissioner for Pacification; court gentlemen vied to enter his gate—on hearing of his coming, Bowen left for another prefecture to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan served as commissioner for pacification, court gentlemen vied to join his faction. On hearing that he was coming, Bowen left for another prefecture to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 除知果州，請罷歲輸瀘南諸州綾絹、絲綿數十萬以寬民力。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Guozhou and requested abolition of the annual delivery of hundreds of thousands of bolts of patterned silk and cotton floss from the southern Luzhou prefectures to ease the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Guozhou and petitioned to abolish the annual levy of hundreds of thousands of bolts of patterned silk and cotton floss from the southern Luzhou prefectures, so as to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 除知興元府、遂寧府、邠州，皆不赴。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Xingyuan, Suining, and Bin prefectures—all of which he did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to govern Xingyuan, Suining, and Bin prefectures, but declined every post.

sentences.zh: 擢提點成都路刑獄，賊史斌破武休，入漢、利，窺劍門，伯溫與成都帥臣盧法原合謀守劍門，賊竟不能入，蜀人德之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to be Judicial Commissioner of the Chengdu circuit; when the bandit Shi Bin broke Wuxiu and entered Han and Li, eying Jianmen Pass, Bowen together with the Chengdu commander Lu Fayuan devised a plan to hold the pass—the bandit could not enter after all, and the people of Shu were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial commissioner of the Chengdu circuit. When the rebel Shi Bin seized Wuxiu and advanced into Han and Li, threatening Jianmen Pass, Bowen and the Chengdu commander Lu Fayuan jointly planned the defense of the pass. The rebels never broke through, and the people of Shu were grateful.

sentences.zh: 除利路轉運副使，提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Transport Commissioner of the Li circuit and promoted to overseer of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice transport commissioner of the Li circuit and made overseer of the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Shaoxing, at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 初，邵雍嘗曰：「世行亂，蜀安，可避居。」

translations.literal: Early on, Shao Yong had said: "When the world falls into disorder, Shu is secure—you can take refuge there."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Shao Yong had said, "When the realm falls into chaos, Shu remains secure. One may take refuge there."

sentences.zh: 及宣和末，伯溫載家使蜀，故免於難。

translations.literal: When the end of Xuanhe came, Bowen moved his household to Shu and thus escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe era, Bowen moved his family to Shu and so escaped the calamity.

sentences.zh: 伯溫嘗論元祐、紹聖之政曰：「公卿大夫，當知國體，以蔡確奸邪，投之死地，何足惜！

translations.literal: Bowen once discussed the governments of Yuanyou and Shaosheng: "Court grandees ought to know the body politic. Cai Que was treacherous and evil—casting him into a dead land is no great loss!
translations.idiomatic: Bowen once remarked on the politics of Yuanyou and Shaoshen: "Grandees of the court ought to understand what the state requires. Cai Que was treacherous and corrupt—sending him to his death is hardly a loss worth mourning!

sentences.zh: 然嘗為宰相，當以宰相待之。

translations.literal: Yet he had once been chief minister and ought to have been treated as a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had once been chief minister and ought to have been treated as one.

sentences.zh: 範忠宣有文正餘風，知國體者也，故欲薄確之罪，言既不用，退而行確詞命，然後求去，君子長者仁人用心也。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongxuan retained Wen Zhengge's legacy and knew the body politic—therefore he wished to lighten Que's punishment; when his words were not used, he retired and then carried out Que's commission documents before seeking leave—a gentleman's and elder's and humane man's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongxuan carried on Wen Zhengge's legacy and understood the needs of state. He therefore wished to mitigate Que's punishment. When his counsel was rejected, he withdrew, carried out Que's appointment documents, and only then sought leave—this was the conduct of a true gentleman and humane elder.

sentences.zh: 確死南荒，豈獨有傷國體哉！

translations.literal: Que died in the southern wilds—was that alone an injury to the body politic!
translations.idiomatic: Que died in the southern wilds—did that not alone wound the dignity of the state!

sentences.zh: 劉摯、梁燾、王岩叟、劉安世忠直有餘，然疾惡已甚，不知國體，以貽後日縉紳之禍，不能無過也。」

translations.literal: Liu Zhi, Liang Zhen, Wang Yansou, and Liu Anshi had surplus loyalty and uprightness, yet they hated evil excessively and did not know the body politic, bequeathing to later generations of court gentlemen the calamity that followed—they too cannot be without fault."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi, Liang Zhen, Wang Yansou, and Liu Anshi had loyalty and integrity to spare, yet they hated evil beyond measure and failed to grasp the needs of state, bequeathing calamity to the court gentlemen who came after. They too were not without fault."

sentences.zh: 趙鼎少從伯溫遊，及當相，乞行追錄，始贈秘閣修撰。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding in his youth had studied with Bowen; when he came to be chief minister, he begged posthumous recognition—only then was Bowen conferred Honorary Compiler of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding had studied with Bowen in his youth. When he became chief minister, he petitioned for posthumous honors, and Bowen was at last granted the title of Honorary Compiler of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘗表伯溫之墓曰：「以學行起元祐，以名節居紹聖，以言廢於崇寧。」

translations.literal: He once inscribed Bowen's tomb: "He rose on learning and conduct in Yuanyou, stood on name and integrity in Shaosheng, and was silenced by speech in Chongning."
translations.idiomatic: He once composed an epitaph for Bowen's tomb: "He rose through learning and conduct in Yuanyou, upheld his name and integrity in Shaosheng, and was silenced for his words in Chongning."

sentences.zh: 世以此三語盡伯溫出處雲。

translations.literal: The world takes these three phrases as fully compassing Bowen's course.
translations.idiomatic: Posterity has taken these three lines as summing up Bowen's entire career.

sentences.zh: 著書有《河南集》、《聞見錄》、《皇極係述》、《辨誣》、《辨惑》、《皇極經世序》、《觀物內外篇解》近百卷。

translations.literal: His writings include nearly a hundred juan: Collected Works of Henan, Records of What Was Heard and Seen, Succession of the Supreme Ultimate, Refutation of Slander, Dispelling Doubt, Preface to the Supreme Ultimate and the Ages of the World, and Exegesis of the Inner and Outer Chapters of Observing Things.
translations.idiomatic: His writings came to nearly a hundred juan, including Collected Works of Henan, Records of What Was Heard and Seen, Succession of the Supreme Ultimate, Refutation of Slander, Dispelling Doubt, Preface to the Supreme Ultimate and the Ages of the World, and Exegesis of the Inner and Outer Chapters of Observing Things.

sentences.zh: 三子：溥、博、傅。

translations.literal: Three sons: Pu, Bo, and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Pu, Bo, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 喻樗，字子才，其先南昌人。

translations.literal: Yu Chu, courtesy name Zicai—his ancestors were men of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chu, whose courtesy name was Zicai, came of a family originally from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 初，俞藥仕梁，位至安州刺史，武帝賜姓喻，後徙嚴，樗其十六世孫也。

translations.literal: Early on, Yu Yao served Liang and rose to Prefect of Anzhou; Emperor Wu of Liang granted the surname Yu; later they moved to Yan—Chu was their sixteenth-generation descendant.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Yu Yao had served the Liang and risen to prefect of Anzhou. Emperor Wu of Liang granted the surname Yu, and the family later moved to Yan. Chu was their sixteenth-generation descendant.

sentences.zh: 少慕伊、洛之學，中建炎三年進士第，為人質直好議論。

translations.literal: In youth he admired the learning of the Yi and Luo schools; in the third year of Jianyan he passed the Jinshi degree. He was plain and straightforward and fond of discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he admired the learning associated with the Yi and Luo traditions. He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Jianyan and was by nature plainspoken and fond of debate.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎去樞筦，居常山，樗往謁，因諷之曰：「公之事上，當使啟沃多而施行少。

translations.literal: When Zhao Ding left the Bureau of Military Affairs and resided in Changshan, Chu went to call on him and obliquely advised: "In serving the sovereign, you ought to make your admonitions many and your implementations few.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ding left the Bureau of Military Affairs and retired to Changshan, Chu called on him and obliquely advised, "In serving the emperor, you should offer much counsel but carry out little yourself.

sentences.zh: 啟沃之際，當使誠意多而語言少。」

translations.literal: In admonishing, you ought to make sincerity much and words few."
translations.idiomatic: When you offer counsel, let sincerity be abundant and words few."

sentences.zh: 鼎奇之，引為上客。

translations.literal: Ding marveled at him and made him a chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was struck by this and took him on as a chief guest.

sentences.zh: 鼎都督川陝、荊襄，辟樗為屬。

translations.literal: When Ding was overall commander of Shaanxi-Sichuan and Jing-Xiang-Huai, he recruited Chu as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding served as overall commander of Shaanxi-Sichuan and Jing-Xiang-Huai, he recruited Chu as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，高宗親征，樗見鼎曰：「六龍臨江，兵氣百倍，然公自度此舉，果出萬全乎？

translations.literal: Early in Shaoxing, the Gaozong Emperor personally campaigned. Chu saw Ding and said: "With the Six Dragons on the river, martial ardor is a hundredfold—yet have you yourself gauged whether this undertaking is truly of ten thousand parts safety?
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaoxing, Gaozong took the field in person. Chu saw Ding and asked, "With the imperial presence on the Yangzi, martial spirit runs high—but do you truly believe this campaign is utterly without risk?

sentences.zh: 或姑試一擲也？」

translations.literal: Or is it perhaps a single throw of the dice?"
translations.idiomatic: Or is it merely a gamble?"

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「中國累年退避不振，敵情益驕，義不可更屈，故讚上行耳。

translations.literal: Ding said: "For years China has retreated without stirring; the enemy grows ever prouder—on principle one cannot bow again, so I supported the sovereign's going forth.
translations.idiomatic: Ding replied, "For years the empire has retreated without rallying, and the enemy grows ever bolder. On principle we cannot bow again, so I supported the emperor's advance.

sentences.zh: 若事之濟否，則非鼎所知也。」

translations.literal: Whether affairs succeed is not something Ding knows."
translations.idiomatic: Whether the venture succeeds is beyond my knowledge."

sentences.zh: 樗曰：「然則當思歸路，毋以賊遺君父憂。」

translations.literal: Chu said: "Then you ought to think of the road home—do not leave the enemy as a worry to lord and father."
translations.idiomatic: Chu said, "Then you must plan the road home and not leave the enemy as a burden on the emperor and the realm."

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「策安出？」

translations.literal: Ding said: "What stratagem do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: Ding asked, "What strategy do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 樗曰：「張德遠有重望，居閩。

translations.literal: Chu said: "Zhang Deyuan has heavy standing and resides in Min.
translations.idiomatic: Chu said, "Zhang Deyuan enjoys great prestige and is now in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 今莫若使其為江、淮、荊、浙、福建等路宣撫使，俾以諸道兵赴闕，命下之日，府庫軍旅錢穀皆得專之。

translations.literal: Now nothing is better than making him Commissioner for Pacification of Jiang, Huai, Jing, Zhe, Fujian, and the rest, enabling him to bring troops of all circuits to court; on the day the order issues, treasuries, armies, and funds may all be at his exclusive disposal.
translations.idiomatic: The best course now is to appoint him commissioner for pacification over the Jiang, Huai, Jing, Zhe, and Fujian circuits, with authority to march the troops of every circuit to the capital. From the day the order is issued, treasuries, armies, and funds should be entirely at his disposal.

sentences.zh: 宣撫來路，即朝廷歸路也。」

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner's route of coming is the court's route of return."
translations.idiomatic: The route by which the commissioner advances is the route by which the court withdraws."

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: Ding said: "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "Very well."

sentences.zh: 於是入奏曰：「今沿江經畫大計略定，非得大臣相應援不可。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entered and memorialized: "The great plan along the river is now broadly set; we cannot do without a great minister to respond in support.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the throne: "The great plan along the river is now largely settled, but we cannot do without a senior minister to coordinate support.

sentences.zh: 如張浚人才，陛下終棄之乎？」

translations.literal: As for talent like Zhang Jun—will Your Majesty finally cast him aside?"
translations.idiomatic: A man of Zhang Jun's ability—will Your Majesty truly leave him unused?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕用之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I shall use him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I shall employ him."

sentences.zh: 遂起浚知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Jun was thereupon summoned to be Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was thereupon recalled to serve as director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 浚至，執鼎手曰：「此行舉措皆合人心。」

translations.literal: When Jun arrived, he took Ding's hand and said: "Every move of this expedition accords with people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: When Jun arrived, he took Ding's hand and said, "Every measure of this campaign has won the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 鼎笑曰：「子才之功也。」

translations.literal: Ding laughed and said: "Zicai's achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Ding laughed and said, "That is Zicai's doing."

sentences.zh: 樗於是往來鼎、浚間，多所裨益。

translations.literal: Chu thereupon went back and forth between Ding and Jun and contributed much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Chu then moved between Ding and Jun and contributed much to their cooperation.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以鼎薦，授秘書省正字兼史館校勘。

translations.literal: Before long, on Ding's recommendation, he was appointed Regular Scribe of the Secretariat with concurrent collation duty in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on Ding's recommendation, he was appointed regular scribe of the Secretariat with concurrent duty as collator in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 初，金既退師，鼎、浚相得歡甚。

translations.literal: Early on, after the Jin had withdrawn, Ding and Jun were on excellent terms.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin armies withdrew, Ding and Jun were on excellent terms.

sentences.zh: 人知其將並相，樗獨言：「二人宜且同在樞府，他日趙退則張繼之。

translations.literal: People knew they would soon both be chancellors; Chu alone said: "The two ought for now to remain together in the Bureau of Military Affairs; later when Zhao retires, Zhang can succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone expected them soon to share the chancellorship, but Chu alone said, "The two should remain together in the Bureau of Military Affairs for now. When Zhao steps down, Zhang can succeed him.

sentences.zh: 立事任人，未甚相遠，則氣脈長。

translations.literal: In establishing affairs and employing men, if they are not far apart, then the vital pulse is long.
translations.idiomatic: If their policies and appointments do not diverge too widely, the political momentum will endure.

sentences.zh: 若同處相位，萬有一不合，或當去位，則必更張，是賢者自相背戾矣。」

translations.literal: If they share the chief ministership and in the slightest should not agree, one must leave office—then they would surely change course; that is worthy men turning against one another."
translations.idiomatic: If they shared the chancellorship and the slightest disagreement arose, one would have to leave office and everything would be overturned—worthy men would end up at odds with one another."

sentences.zh: 後稍如其言。

translations.literal: Later matters went somewhat as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Events later unfolded much as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 又嘗曰：「推車者遇艱險則相詬病，及車之止也，則欣然如初。

translations.literal: He also once said: "Those who push a cart, when they meet hardship, reproach one another; when the cart stops, they are cheerful as at first.
translations.idiomatic: He also once said, "Men pushing a cart reproach one another when the road grows hard, but once the cart stops, they are cheerful again as before.

sentences.zh: 士之於國家亦若是而已。」

translations.literal: Gentlemen toward the state are just the same."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars toward the state are no different."

sentences.zh: 初，樗善鑒識，宣和間，謂其友人沈晦試進士當第一。

translations.literal: Early on, Chu was skilled at judgment; in the Xuanhe era he told his friend Shen Hui that in the Jinshi examination he would rank first.
translations.idiomatic: Chu had a gift for judging men. During Xuanhe he told his friend Shen Hui that he would rank first in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，又謂今歲進士張九成當第一，淩景夏次之。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyan he again said that this year's Jinshi Zhang Jiucheng would rank first and Ling Jingxia second.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan he predicted that Zhang Jiucheng would rank first among the jinshi that year and Ling Jingxia second.

sentences.zh: 會風折大槐，樗以作二簡遺之，後果然。

translations.literal: When a great locust tree was broken in a windstorm, Chu made two slips and sent them to them—later it turned out indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: When a great locust tree was broken in a storm, Chu composed two slips and sent them to the candidates. Later events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎嘗以樊光遠免舉事訪樗，樗曰：「今年省試不可無此人。」

translations.literal: Zhao Ding once consulted Chu about exempting Fan Guangyuan from the examination; Chu said: "This year's provincial examination cannot lack this man."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding once consulted Chu about exempting Fan Guangyuan from the examination. Chu said, "This year's provincial examination cannot do without this man."

sentences.zh: 於是光遠亦第一。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guangyuan also ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan indeed ranked first.

sentences.zh: 初，樗二女方擇配，富人交請婚，不許。

translations.literal: Early on, when Chu's two daughters were choosing husbands, the rich vied to request marriage—he did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu's two daughters were choosing husbands, wealthy families vied to propose marriage, but he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 及見汪洋、張孝祥，乃曰「佳婿也。」

translations.literal: When he saw Wang Yang and Zhang Xiaoxiang, he said: "Fine sons-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: When he met Wang Yang and Zhang Xiaoxiang, he declared, "These will make fine sons-in-law."

sentences.zh: 遂以妻之。

translations.literal: He then gave them his daughters in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them his daughters in marriage.

sentences.zh: 洪興祖

translations.literal: Hong Xingzu
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xingzu

sentences.zh: 洪興祖，字慶善，鎮江丹陽人。

translations.literal: Hong Xingzu, courtesy name Qingshan, was a native of Danyang in Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xingzu, whose courtesy name was Qingshan, came from Danyang in Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 少讀《禮》至《中庸》，頓悟性命之理，績文日進。

translations.literal: In youth he read the Rites as far as the Doctrine of the Mean and suddenly awakened to the principle of nature and destiny; his literary composition advanced daily.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he read the Rites through to the Doctrine of the Mean and suddenly grasped the principles of nature and destiny. His writing improved day by day.

sentences.zh: 登政和上舍第，為湖州士曹，改宣教郎。

translations.literal: He passed the upper-college degree in the Zhenghe era, served as Clerk for Scholars in Huzhou, and was changed to Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the upper-college examination in the Zhenghe era, served as clerk for scholars in Huzhou, and was promoted to instructor.

sentences.zh: 高宗時在揚州，庶事草創，選人改秩軍頭司引見，自興祖始。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor was at Yangzhou and all affairs were newly established, candidates changing rank were first presented through the Army Head Office—Xingzu was the first.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was at Yangzhou and the government was still being formed, candidates changing rank were first presented through the Army Head Office—Xingzu was the first.

sentences.zh: 召試，授秘書省正字，後為太常博士。

translations.literal: He was summoned for examination and appointed Regular Scribe of the Secretariat; later he became Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for examination, he was appointed regular scribe of the Secretariat and later became a doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 上疏乞收人心，納謀策，安民情，壯國威。

translations.literal: He memorialized begging to gather people's hearts, accept stratagems, settle the people's feelings, and strengthen the state's majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial urging the court to win back popular loyalty, heed counsel, reassure the people, and strengthen national prestige.

sentences.zh: 又論國家再造，一宜以藝祖為法。

translations.literal: He also discussed the state's renewal and said that above all one ought to take Founder Taizu as model.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that in rebuilding the state, the court ought above all to take Taizu as its model.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，蘇、湖地震。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, Suzhou and Huzhou suffered earthquakes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, Suzhou and Huzhou were struck by earthquakes.

sentences.zh: 興祖時為駕部郎官，應詔上疏，具言朝廷紀綱之失，為時宰所惡，主管太平觀。

translations.literal: Xingzu was then Director of the Transport Office; by imperial order he memorialized, setting forth in detail the court's failures of discipline and regulation, and was hated by the chief ministers—he was put in charge of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu was then director of the Transport Office. By imperial order he memorialized, detailing the court's failures of discipline and regulation. The chief ministers took offense, and he was assigned to oversee the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 起知廣德軍，視水原為陂塘六百餘所，民無旱憂。

translations.literal: He was raised to be Prefect of Guangde Army, surveyed the water sources and made more than six hundred reservoir ponds, and the people had no fear of drought.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Guangde Army, surveyed the water sources, and built more than six hundred reservoir ponds so that the people no longer feared drought.

sentences.zh: 一新學舍，因定從祀：自十哲曾子而下七十有一人，又列先儒左丘明而下二十有六人。

translations.literal: He renovated the schoolhouse and thereby fixed the accompanying sacrifices: from the Ten Sages and Zengzi downward, seventy-one persons; and he also listed the early Confucians from Zuo Qiuming downward, twenty-six persons.
translations.idiomatic: He renovated the school and fixed the accompanying sacrifices: from the Ten Sages and Zengzi downward, seventy-one persons, and from the early Confucians beginning with Zuo Qiuming, twenty-six persons.

sentences.zh: 擢提點江東刑獄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to be Judicial Commissioner of the Jiangdong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial commissioner of the Jiangdong circuit.

sentences.zh: 知真州。

translations.literal: He became Prefect of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 州當兵衝，瘡痍未瘳。

translations.literal: The prefecture lay on a military thoroughfare and its wounds were not yet healed.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay on a military thoroughfare, and its wounds had not yet healed.

sentences.zh: 興祖始至，請復一年租，從之。

translations.literal: When Xingzu first arrived, he requested restoration of one year's rent, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzu first arrived, he petitioned to remit one year's rent, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年再請，又從之。

translations.literal: The next year he requested again, and again it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he petitioned again, and again the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是流民復業，墾辟荒田至七萬餘畝。

translations.literal: From this, displaced people returned to their occupations and reclaimed wasteland reaching more than seventy thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter displaced people returned to their fields and reclaimed more than seventy thousand mu of wasteland.

sentences.zh: 徙知饒州，先夢持六刀，覺曰：「三刀為益，今倍之，其饒乎？」

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Prefect of Raozhou. He had earlier dreamed of holding six knives and on waking said: "Three knives make Yi—now doubled, is it not Rao?"
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Raozhou. He had dreamed of holding six knives and on waking said, "Three knives form the character for 'benefit'; doubled, does this not spell 'Rao'?"

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it proved so.

sentences.zh: 是時秦檜當國，諫官多檜門下，爭彈劾以媚檜。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Hui held power; remonstrating officials were mostly from Hui's faction and vied to impeach others to please him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin Hui dominated the government. Most remonstrating officials belonged to his faction and competed to impeach others to win his favor.

sentences.zh: 興祖坐嘗作故龍圖閣學士程瑀《論語解序》，語涉怨望，編管昭州，卒，年六十有六。

translations.literal: Xingzu was punished because he had once written a preface to the former Academician Expositor Cheng Yu's Exegesis of the Analects, with language touching on resentment—he was banished to supervise Zhaozhou and died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu was punished because he had written a preface to the former Academician Expositor Cheng Yu's Exegesis of the Analects containing language deemed resentful. He was banished to Zhaozhou, where he died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔復其官，直敷文閣。

translations.literal: The next year an edict restored his office and conferred the title of Direct Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict restored his office and conferred upon him the title of Direct Academician Expositor.

sentences.zh: 興祖好古博學，自少至老，未嘗一日去書。

translations.literal: Xingzu loved antiquity and was broadly learned; from youth to old age he never went a day without books.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu loved antiquity and was broadly learned. From youth to old age he never went a day without books.

sentences.zh: 著《老莊本旨》、《周易通義》、《係辭要旨》、《古文孝經序讚》、《離騷楚詞考異》行於世。

translations.literal: His writings include Original Purport of Laozi and Zhuangzi, Comprehensive Meaning of the Book of Changes, Essential Purport of the Appended Phrases, Preface and Praise of the Old Text Classic of Filial Piety, and Critical Variants of the Songs of Chu and Li sao, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works—including Original Purport of Laozi and Zhuangzi, Comprehensive Meaning of the Book of Changes, Essential Purport of the Appended Phrases, Preface and Praise of the Old Text Classic of Filial Piety, and Critical Variants of the Songs of Chu and Li sao—circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 高閌，字抑崇，明州鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Gao Kang, courtesy name Yichong, was a native of Yin County in Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kang, whose courtesy name was Yichong, came from Yin County in Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，以上舍選賜進士第。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, on selection from the upper college he was granted the Jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing he was granted the jinshi degree on selection from the upper college.

sentences.zh: 執政薦之，召為秘書省正字。

translations.literal: The chief ministers recommended him and he was summoned to be Regular Scribe of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers recommended him, and he was summoned to serve as regular scribe of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時將賜新進士《儒行》、《中庸》篇，閌奏《儒行》詞說不醇，請止賜《中庸》，庶幾學者得知聖學淵源，而不惑於他說，從之。

translations.literal: At the time the court was about to bestow on new Jinshi the Confucian Conduct and Doctrine of the Mean chapters. Kang memorialized that the language of Confucian Conduct was not pure and begged that only the Doctrine of the Mean be given, so that scholars might know the deep source of sage learning and not be confused by other doctrines—it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court was about to bestow on new jinshi graduates the Confucian Conduct and Doctrine of the Mean. Kang memorialized that the language of Confucian Conduct was impure and asked that only the Doctrine of the Mean be granted, so scholars might know the deep source of sage learning without being misled by other doctrines. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 權禮部員外郎兼史館校勘。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent collation duty in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting vice minister of rites with concurrent duty as collator in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 麵對，言：「《春秋》之法，莫大於正名。

translations.literal: In audience he said: "In the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, nothing is greater than rectifying names.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said, "In the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, nothing is greater than rectifying names.

sentences.zh: 今樞密院號本兵柄，而諸路軍馬盡屬都督，是朝廷兵柄自分為二。

translations.literal: Now the Bureau of Military Affairs is styled as holding the root of military power, yet the armies of all circuits belong entirely to the overall commander—thus the court's military authority is divided in two.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs is said to hold the root of military power, yet the armies of all circuits belong entirely to the overall commander. The court's military authority is thus split in two.

sentences.zh: 又周六卿，其大事則從其長，小事官屬猶得專達。

translations.literal: Again, in the six ministries of Zhou, on great affairs they followed the head, while on small affairs subordinates might still report directly.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou six ministries, on great affairs they followed the department head, while on small matters subordinates could still report directly.

sentences.zh: 今一切拘以文法，雖利害灼然可見，官長且不敢自決，必請於朝，故廟堂之事益繁，而省曹官屬乃與胥吏無異。

translations.literal: Now everything is bound by written regulations; even when benefit and harm are plainly visible, the department head dares not decide for himself but must request the court—thus court affairs grow ever more numerous, while provincial officials are no different from clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Today everything is bound by written regulations. Even when benefit and harm are plainly visible, the department head dares not decide alone but must seek the court's approval. Court business grows ever heavier, while provincial officials are reduced to the status of clerks.

sentences.zh: 又政事之行，給、舍得繳駁，台諫得論列，若給、舍以為然，台諫以為不然，則不容不改。

translations.literal: Again, in the execution of policy, the Secretariat and Chancellery may return documents for reconsideration and the censorate may debate them; if the Secretariat and Chancellery approve but the censorate disapproves, then it cannot but be changed.
translations.idiomatic: In executing policy, the Secretariat and Chancellery may return documents for reconsideration and the censorate may debate them. If the Secretariat approves but the censorate objects, the measure cannot stand unchanged.

sentences.zh: 祖宗時有繳駁台諫章疏不以為嫌者，恐其得於風聞，致朝廷之有過舉。

translations.literal: In ancestral times there were cases where returned memorials from the censorate were not regarded as offensive, lest they gain something from hearsay and cause the court to err.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founders there were cases where returned censorial memorials were not taken as offensive, lest the censors, hearing rumors, cause the court to err.

sentences.zh: 然此風不見久矣，臣恐朝廷之權反在台諫。

translations.literal: Yet this practice has long been absent; I fear the court's authority has shifted instead to the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: That practice has long vanished. I fear the court's authority has shifted instead to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 且祖宗時，監察御史許言事，靖康中嘗行之。

translations.literal: Moreover, in ancestral times investigating censors were permitted to speak on affairs; this was once practiced in the Jingkang period.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under the founders investigating censors were permitted to speak on affairs—a practice briefly revived in the Jingkang period.

sentences.zh: 今則名為台官，實無言責，此皆名之未正也。」

translations.literal: Now they are called censorial officials in name but in fact bear no duty of speech—these are all cases where names have not been rectified."
translations.idiomatic: Today they are called censors in name but bear no real duty to speak. These are all failures to rectify names."

sentences.zh: 尋遷著作佐郎，以言者論罷，主管崇道觀。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Assistant Compiler, but on the censors' argument was dismissed and put in charge of the Chongdao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to assistant compiler, but censors attacked him and he was dismissed to oversee the Chongdao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 召為國子司業。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 時興太學，閌奏宜先經術，帝曰：「士習詩賦已久，遽能使之通經乎？」

translations.literal: At the time the Imperial University was being expanded. Kang memorialized that classical learning ought to come first. The Emperor said: "Scholars have practiced poetry and fu for a long time—can they suddenly be made to master the classics?"
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University was being expanded. Kang urged that classical learning come first. The emperor said, "Scholars have practiced poetry and fu for so long—can they suddenly be made to master the classics?"

sentences.zh: 閌曰：「先王設太學，惟講經術而已。

translations.literal: Kang said: "The Former Kings established the Imperial University solely for lecturing on classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Kang replied, "The former kings established the Imperial University solely to teach the classics.

sentences.zh: 國初猶循唐制用詩賦，神宗始以經術造士，遂罷詩賦，又慮不足以盡人才，乃設詞學一科。

translations.literal: At the founding the Tang system of poetry and fu was still followed; Emperor Shenzong first used classical learning to form scholars and abolished poetry and fu, yet fearing this was insufficient to exhaust talent, he established the belles-lettres subject.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding the Tang system of poetry and fu was still followed. Shenzong first used the classics to form scholars and abolished poetry and fu, yet fearing this would not exhaust talent, he established the belles-lettres subject.

sentences.zh: 今宜以經義為主，而加詩賦。」

translations.literal: Now one ought to take classical meaning as primary and add poetry and fu."
translations.idiomatic: Now the classics should be primary, with poetry and fu added."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 閌於是條具以聞。

translations.literal: Kang thereupon set forth the details in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Kang thereupon submitted a detailed memorial.

sentences.zh: 其法以《六經》、《語》、《孟》義為一場，詩賦次之，子史論又次之，時務策又次之。

translations.literal: The method took exegesis of the Six Classics, Analects, and Mencius as one session, poetry and fu next, essays on the masters and histories next, and current-affairs policy questions last.
translations.idiomatic: The method placed exegesis of the Six Classics, Analects, and Mencius in the first session, poetry and fu second, essays on the masters and histories third, and current-affairs policy questions last.

sentences.zh: 太學課試及郡國科舉，盡以此為法，且立郡國士補國學監生之制。

translations.literal: University examinations and prefectural and circuit civil-service examinations all used this method, and a system was also established for prefectural scholars to enter the university as supervising students.
translations.idiomatic: University examinations and prefectural civil-service examinations all followed this method, and a system was established for prefectural scholars to enter the university as supervising students.

sentences.zh: 中興已後學製，多閌所建明。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, much of the academic system was what Kang had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, much of the academic system was of Kang's devising.

sentences.zh: 閌又言建學之始，宜得老成以誘掖後進。

translations.literal: Kang also said that in establishing learning one ought to obtain mature men to guide and encourage the young.
translations.idiomatic: Kang also said that in founding the university the court ought to obtain mature scholars to guide the young.

sentences.zh: 乃薦全州文學師維藩，詔除國子錄。

translations.literal: He thereupon recommended Wei Weifan, Instructor of Letters in Quanzhou, and an edict appointed him Recorder of the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Wei Weifan, instructor of letters in Quanzhou, who was appointed recorder of the Directorate by edict.

sentences.zh: 維藩，眉山人，精《春秋》學，林栗其高第也，故首薦之。

translations.literal: Weifan, a man of Meizhou, was expert in Spring and Autumn learning; Lin Li was his top student—therefore he was first recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Weifan of Meizhou was expert in Spring and Autumn learning. Lin Li had been his top student, and so he was recommended first.

sentences.zh: 新學成，閌奏補試者六千人，且乞臨雍，繼率諸生上表以請。

translations.literal: When the new university was completed, Kang memorialized that six thousand candidates sat for the qualifying examination, and begged that the emperor visit the university; he then led the students in submitting a memorial to request it.
translations.idiomatic: When the new university was completed, Kang reported that six thousand candidates sat for the qualifying examination and begged the emperor to visit the university. He then led the students in submitting a memorial requesting the visit.

sentences.zh: 於是帝幸太學，秦熺執經，閌講《易·泰卦》，賜三品服。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor visited the Imperial University; Qin Xi lectured on the classics and Kang expounded the Tai hexagram of the Book of Changes, and he was granted third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then visited the Imperial University. Qin Xi lectured on the classics while Kang expounded the Tai hexagram, and Kang was granted robes of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 胡寅聞之，以書責閌曰：「閣下為師儒之首，不能建大論，明天人之理，乃阿諛柄臣，希合風旨，求舉太平之典，欺天罔人孰甚焉！

translations.literal: When Hu Yin heard of this, he wrote reproaching Kang: "Your Excellency stands at the head of the teacher-scholars yet cannot establish a great argument or clarify the principle of Heaven and man; instead you flatter a powerful minister, conforming to the prevailing tone, seeking to perform the ceremony of the Great Peace—who deceives Heaven and man more than this!
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Yin heard of this, he wrote to reproach Kang: "You stand at the head of the teacher-scholars yet cannot establish a great argument or clarify the principle of Heaven and man. Instead you flatter a powerful minister and conform to the prevailing tone, seeking to perform the ceremony of the Great Peace. Who deceives Heaven and man more than this?

sentences.zh: 平生誌行掃地矣。」

translations.literal: Your life's resolve and conduct are swept to the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Your life's resolve and conduct are swept to the ground."

sentences.zh: 閌少宗程頤學。

translations.literal: Kang in youth revered the learning of Cheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Kang revered the learning of Cheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，楊時為祭酒，閌為諸生。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe, Yang Shi was Libationer and Kang was a student.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xuanhe, Yang Shi served as libationer and Kang was among his students.

sentences.zh: 胡安國至京師，訪士於時，以閌為首稱，由是知名。

translations.literal: When Hu An'guo came to the capital, he sought scholars through Shi and ranked Kang first—thereby he became known.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu An'guo came to the capital, he sought scholars through Yang Shi and ranked Kang first. Thereby Kang became known.

sentences.zh: 閌除禮部侍郎，帝因問閌張九成安否，明日，復以問秦檜，檜疑閌薦，中丞李文會承檜旨劾閌，出知筠州，不赴，卒。

translations.literal: Kang was appointed Vice Minister of Rites. The Emperor thereupon asked Kang whether Zhang Jiucheng was safe; the next day he asked Qin Hui again. Hui suspected Kang of recommending Zhang. The Vice Censor Li Wenhuai, following Hui's intent, impeached Kang. Kang was sent out to be Prefect of Yunzhou, did not go, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was appointed vice minister of rites. The emperor asked whether Zhang Jiucheng was safe; the next day he asked Qin Hui again. Hui suspected Kang of recommending Zhang. Vice Censor Li Wenhuai, following Hui's intent, impeached Kang, who was sent out as prefect of Yunzhou. He did not take up the post and died.

sentences.zh: 初，秦棣嘗使姚孚請婚，閌辭之。

translations.literal: Early on, Qin Di had sent Yao Fu to request marriage, and Kang declined.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Qin Di had sent Yao Fu to propose marriage, but Kang declined.

sentences.zh: 其著述有《春秋集傳》行於世。

translations.literal: His writings include Collected Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 程大昌

translations.literal: Cheng Dachang
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Dachang

sentences.zh: 程大昌，字泰之，徽州休寧人。

translations.literal: Cheng Dachang, courtesy name Taizhi, was a native of Xiuning in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Dachang, whose courtesy name was Taizhi, came from Xiuning in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 十歲能屬文，登紹興二十一年進士第。

translations.literal: At ten he could compose prose; he passed the Jinshi degree in the twenty-first year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could compose prose. He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-first year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 主吳縣簿，未上，丁父憂。

translations.literal: He was appointed Clerk of Wu County but had not yet reported when he mourned his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed clerk of Wu County but had not yet reported for duty when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服除，著十論言當世事，獻於朝，宰相湯思退奇之，擢太平州教授。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he composed ten discourses on current affairs and presented them to the court; Chief Minister Tang Sirui marveled at them and promoted him to Professor of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he composed ten discourses on current affairs and presented them to court. Chief Minister Tang Sirui was impressed and appointed him professor in Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，召為太學正，試館職，為秘書省正字。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned to be Director of the Imperial University, tested for a library post, and made Regular Scribe of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned as director of the Imperial University, tested for a library post, and appointed regular scribe of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong acceded, he was transferred to Assistant Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong acceded, he was transferred to assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝初政，銳意事功，命令四出，貴近或預密議。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was beginning his reign and keenly pursued achievement; orders issued in all directions, and those close to him sometimes took part in secret deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was beginning his reign and keenly pursued achievement. Orders issued in all directions, and those close to him sometimes joined secret deliberations.

sentences.zh: 會詔百官言事，大昌奏曰：「漢石顯知元帝信己，先請夜開宮門之詔。

translations.literal: When an edict called on all officials to speak, Dachang memorialized: "In Han, Shi Xian, knowing that Emperor Yuan trusted him, first requested an edict to open the palace gates at night.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called on all officials to speak, Dachang memorialized: "In Han, Shi Xian, knowing that Emperor Yuan trusted him, first requested an edict to open the palace gates at night.

sentences.zh: 他日，故夜還，稱詔啟關，或言矯製，帝笑以前詔示之。

translations.literal: Another day he returned at night, claimed the edict to open the gate, and some said it was a forged order; the Emperor laughed and showed them the earlier edict.
translations.idiomatic: Another night he returned and claimed the edict to open the gate. Some said it was forged, but the emperor laughed and showed them the earlier edict.

sentences.zh: 自是顯真矯製，人不復言。

translations.literal: From this Xian truly forged orders and no one spoke again.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Xian truly forged orders, and no one dared speak again.

sentences.zh: 國朝命令必由三省，防此弊也。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's commands must pass through the Three Departments—this guards against that abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's commands must pass through the Three Departments—this guards against that abuse.

sentences.zh: 請自今被御前直降文書，皆申省審奏乃得行，以合祖宗之規，以防石顯之奸。」

translations.literal: I beg that from now on all documents directly descending from before the throne be submitted to the departments for review and memorial before they may be executed, to accord with ancestral regulation and guard against Shi Xian's treachery."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that hereafter all documents descending directly from the throne be submitted to the departments for review before execution, to accord with ancestral regulation and guard against Shi Xian's treachery."

sentences.zh: 又言：「去歲完顏亮入寇，無一士死守，而兵將至今策勳未已。

translations.literal: He also said: "Last year Wanyan Liang invaded, yet not a single scholar held fast in death while soldiers and generals to this day still plot merit—
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Last year Wanyan Liang invaded, yet not a single scholar died defending his post, while soldiers and generals still plot merit to this day—

sentences.zh: 惟李寶捷膠西，虞允文戰采石，實屠亮之階。

translations.literal: only Li Bao's victory at Jiaoxi and Yu Yunwen's battle at Caishi truly cut off the steps by which Liang might ascend.
translations.idiomatic: only Li Bao's victory at Jiaoxi and Yu Yunwen's battle at Caishi truly cut off Liang's path to success.

sentences.zh: 今寶罷兵，允文守夔，此公論所謂不平也。」

translations.literal: Now Bao has been removed from command and Yunwen guards Kui—this is what public opinion calls unfair."
translations.idiomatic: Now Bao has been removed from command while Yunwen guards Kui—this is what public opinion calls unfair."

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，選為恭王府讚讀。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised it and selected him as Reader for the Prince of Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this and appointed him reader for the Prince of Gong.

sentences.zh: 遷國子司業兼權禮部侍郎、直學士院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education with concurrent acting Vice Minister of Rites and Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Directorate of Education with concurrent acting vice minister of rites and academician expositor.

sentences.zh: 帝問大昌曰：「朕治道不進，奈何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Dachang: "My way of governance does not advance—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Dachang, "My governance does not advance—what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 大昌對曰：「陛下勤儉過古帝王，自女真通和，知尊中國，不可謂無效。

translations.literal: Dachang replied: "Your Majesty's diligence and frugality surpass the ancient emperors. Since peace with the Jurchen, they know to honor China—this cannot be called without effect.
translations.idiomatic: Dachang replied, "Your Majesty's diligence and frugality surpass the ancient emperors. Since peace with the Jurchen, they know to honor China—that cannot be called without effect.

sentences.zh: 但當求賢納諫，修政事，則大有為之業在其中，不必他求奇策，以幸速成。」

translations.literal: One has only to seek the worthy and accept remonstrance and repair government—then the great enterprise of full achievement lies within this; there is no need to seek strange stratagems in hope of rapid success."
translations.idiomatic: You need only seek worthy men, accept remonstrance, and repair government. The great enterprise lies therein; there is no need to seek strange stratagems for rapid success."

sentences.zh: 又言：「淮上築城太多，緩急何人可守？

translations.literal: He also said: "Too many fortresses are being built on the Huai—if urgency arises, who can hold them?
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Too many fortresses are being built on the Huai—if crisis comes, who can hold them?

sentences.zh: 設險莫如練卒，練卒莫如擇將。」

translations.literal: In establishing defenses nothing surpasses drilling troops; in drilling troops nothing surpasses choosing generals."
translations.idiomatic: In establishing defenses nothing surpasses drilling troops; in drilling troops nothing surpasses choosing generals."

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 除浙東提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was appointed Judicial Commissioner of the Zhedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial commissioner of the Zhedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 會歲豐，酒稅逾額，有挾朝命請增額者，大昌力拒之，曰：「大昌寧罪去，不可增也。」

translations.literal: In a year of abundance the wine tax exceeded the quota; some, bearing court orders, requested an increase. Dachang firmly refused and said: "Dachang would rather be punished and leave than allow an increase."
translations.idiomatic: In a year of abundance the wine tax exceeded the quota. Some, bearing court orders, requested an increase. Dachang firmly refused: "I would rather be punished and leave than allow an increase."

sentences.zh: 徙江西轉運副使，大昌曰：「可以興利去害，行吾誌矣。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Transport Commissioner of the Jiangxi circuit. Dachang said: "I can promote benefit and remove harm and carry out my resolve."
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice transport commissioner of Jiangxi. Dachang said, "Here I can promote benefit, remove harm, and carry out my resolve."

sentences.zh: 會歲歉，出錢十餘萬緡，代輸吉、贛、臨江、南安夏稅折帛。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he disbursed more than a hundred thousand strings of cash to pay on behalf of the summer tax in silk of Ji, Gan, Linjiang, and Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he disbursed more than a hundred thousand strings of cash to pay the summer tax in silk for Ji, Gan, Linjiang, and Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 清江縣舊有破坑、桐塘二堰，以捍江護田及民居，地幾二千頃。

translations.literal: Qingjiang County formerly had the Po Pit and Tongtang weirs to hold back the river and protect fields and dwellings—nearly two thousand qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: Qingjiang County formerly had the Po Pit and Tongtang weirs to hold back the river and protect fields and dwellings—nearly two thousand qing of land.

sentences.zh: 後堰壞，歲罹水患且四十年，大昌力復其舊。

translations.literal: Later the weirs collapsed and for nearly forty years the region suffered flood calamity; Dachang strenuously restored them to their former state.
translations.idiomatic: Later the weirs collapsed, and for nearly forty years the region suffered floods. Dachang strenuously restored them.

sentences.zh: 進秘閣修撰，召為秘書少監，帝勞之曰：「卿，朕所簡記。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Honorary Compiler of the Secretariat and summoned to be Vice Director of the Secretariat. The Emperor comforted him: "You are one I have noted.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to honorary compiler of the Secretariat and summoned as vice director of the Secretariat. The emperor said to him, "You are one I have marked for notice.

sentences.zh: 監司若人人如卿，朕何憂？」

translations.literal: If every circuit commissioner were like you, what would I have to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: If every circuit commissioner were like you, what would I have to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was given concurrent appointment as Drafting Academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was given concurrent appointment as drafting academician of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六和塔寺僧以鎮潮為功，求內降給賜所置田產仍免科徭，大昌奏：「僧寺既違法置田，又移科徭於民，奈何許之！

translations.literal: Monks of the Liuhe Pagoda Temple, claiming merit in calming the tide, sought an inner descent granting the fields the temple had illegally acquired and still exempting them from tax and corvée. Dachang memorialized: "The temple has both illegally acquired fields and shifted tax and corvée onto the people—how can this be permitted!
translations.idiomatic: Monks of the Liuhe Pagoda Temple, claiming merit in calming the tide, sought an imperial grant of fields the temple had illegally acquired, with tax and corvée still shifted onto the people. Dachang memorialized, "The temple has illegally acquired fields and shifted burdens onto the people—how can this be permitted!

sentences.zh: 況自修塔之後，潮果不齧岸乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, since the pagoda was repaired, has the tide truly ceased gnawing the bank?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the pagoda was repaired, has the tide truly ceased eroding the bank?"

sentences.zh: 寢其命。

translations.literal: He shelved the order.
translations.idiomatic: He shelved the order.

sentences.zh: 權刑部侍郎，升侍講兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Justice and promoted to Lecturer-in-Attendance with concurrent Libationer of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting vice minister of justice and promoted to lecturer-in-attendance with concurrent libationer of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 大昌言：「辟以止辟，未聞縱有罪為仁也。

translations.literal: Dachang said: "Punishment is used to stop punishment—one has never heard that pardoning the guilty is benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Dachang said, "Punishment exists to end punishment—no one has ever heard that pardoning the guilty counts as benevolence.

sentences.zh: 今四方讞獄例擬貸死，臣謂有司當守法，人主察其可貸則貸之。

translations.literal: Now in criminal cases throughout the realm the usual proposal is to commute death—your servant holds that the officials ought to keep the law, and the sovereign may pardon when he sees fit.
translations.idiomatic: Today criminal cases everywhere are routinely proposed for commutation of death. I hold that officials should uphold the law, and the sovereign may pardon when he sees fit.

sentences.zh: 如此，則法伸乎下，仁歸乎上矣。」

translations.literal: In this way the law extends below and benevolence returns above."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the law will prevail below and benevolence will reside above."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 兼給事中。

translations.literal: He was given concurrent appointment as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was given concurrent appointment as supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 江陵都統製率逢原縱部曲毆百姓，守帥辛棄疾以言狀徙帥江西。

translations.literal: The overall commander of Jiangling, Lü Fengyuan, let his troops beat the common people; the defending commander Xin Qiji reported the facts and had Fengyuan transferred to command in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The overall commander of Jiangling, Lü Fengyuan, allowed his troops to beat commoners. The defending commander Xin Qiji reported the facts and had Fengyuan transferred to command in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 大昌因極論「自此屯戍州郡，不可為矣」！

translations.literal: Dachang thereupon argued forcefully that "from this on, garrisoning prefectures and circuits cannot be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Dachang argued forcefully that from this point on, garrisoning prefectures and circuits would be impossible.

sentences.zh: 逢原由是坐削兩官，降本軍副將。

translations.literal: Fengyuan was thereby punished by reduction of two ranks and demotion to deputy general of his original army.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyuan was punished by reduction of two ranks and demotion to deputy general of his original army.

sentences.zh: 累遷權吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 言：「今日諸軍，西北舊人日少，其子孫伉健者，當教之戰陣。

translations.literal: He said: "In the armies of today, the old men of the northwest grow fewer day by day; where their sons and grandsons are sturdy, they ought to be taught battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "In today's armies the old northwestern soldiers grow fewer by the day. Where their sons and grandsons are sturdy, they should be taught battle formations.

sentences.zh: 不宜輕聽離軍。

translations.literal: One ought not lightly permit them to leave the army.
translations.idiomatic: They should not lightly be allowed to leave the army.

sentences.zh: 且禁衛之士，祖宗非獨以備宿衛而已，南征北伐，是嘗為先鋒。

translations.literal: Moreover, the guards of the forbidden precinct—the founders did not regard them solely as preparing night watch. In southern campaigns and northern expeditions they were once the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the forbidden guards were not established by the founders solely for night watch. In southern and northern campaigns they were once the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 今率三年輒補外，用違其長，既有征行，無人在選。

translations.literal: Now generally after three years they are posted outside, using them against their strengths; when campaigns arise, no one remains for selection.
translations.idiomatic: Now after three years they are generally posted outside, misusing their strengths. When campaigns arise, no capable men remain for selection.

sentences.zh: 奈何始以材武擇之，而終以庸常棄之乎？

translations.literal: How can one first select them for martial talent and in the end discard them as mediocre?
translations.idiomatic: How can we first select them for martial talent and in the end discard them as mediocre?

sentences.zh: 願留三衙勿遣。」

translations.literal: I beg that the Three Yamen guards not be dispatched."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Three Yamen guards not be dispatched."

sentences.zh: 會行中外更迭之制，力請郡，遂出知泉州。

translations.literal: When the system of alternating inner and outer appointments was implemented, he strenuously requested a prefecture and was sent out to be Prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the system of alternating inner and outer appointments was implemented, he strenuously requested a prefectural post and was sent out as prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 汀州賊沈師作亂，戍將蕭統領與戰死，閩部大震。

translations.literal: The bandit Shen Shi of Tingzhou rebelled; the garrison commander Xiao Tong led troops and died in battle, and the Min region was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Shen Shi rebelled in Tingzhou. The garrison commander Xiao Tong led troops and died in battle, and the Min region was greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 漕檄統製裴師武討之。

translations.literal: The transport office ordered Overall Commander Pei Shiwu to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The transport office ordered Overall Commander Pei Shiwu to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 師武以未得帥符不行，大昌手書趣之曰：「事急矣，有如帥責君，可持吾書自解。」

translations.literal: Shiwu, not having received the commander's order, would not go. Dachang wrote him by hand urging: "The affair is urgent. If the commander blames you, you may use my letter to explain yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Shiwu would not move without the commander's order. Dachang wrote urging him: "The affair is urgent. If the commander blames you, use my letter to explain yourself."

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊謀攻城，而先使諜者衷甲縱火為內應。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits planned to attack the city and first sent spies to wear armor inside and set fires as internal response.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits planned to attack the city and first sent spies to wear armor within and set fires as an internal signal.

sentences.zh: 會師武軍至，復得諜者，賊遂散去。

translations.literal: When Shiwu's army arrived, they again captured spies and the bandits thereupon dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiwu's army arrived, spies were captured again and the bandits dispersed.

sentences.zh: 遷知建寧府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Prefect of Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be prefect of Jianning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 光宗嗣位，徙知明州，尋奉祠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded, he was moved to be Prefect of Mingzhou and soon took leave for temple service.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong succeeded, he was moved to Mingzhou and soon took leave for temple service.

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年，請老，以龍圖閣學士致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxi he requested old age and retired with the title of Academician Expositor of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxi he requested retirement and left office with the title of Academician Expositor of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年卒，年七十三，諡文簡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingyuan he died, aged seventy-three; his posthumous title was Wenhian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingyuan he died at seventy-three. His posthumous title was Wenhian.

sentences.zh: 大昌篤學，於古今事靡不考究。

translations.literal: Dachang was devoted to learning and investigated exhaustively the affairs of antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: Dachang was devoted to learning and investigated exhaustively affairs ancient and modern.

sentences.zh: 有《禹貢論》、《易原》、《雍錄》、《易老通言》、《考古編》、《演繁露》、《北邊備對》行於世。

translations.literal: His writings include Discourse on the Tribute of Yu, Origins of the Changes, Record of Yong, Comprehensive Words on the Changes and Laozi, Collected Archaeological Studies, Extended Explanations, and Northern Frontier Preparedness, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works—including Discourse on the Tribute of Yu, Origins of the Changes, Record of Yong, Comprehensive Words on the Changes and Laozi, Collected Archaeological Studies, Extended Explanations, and Northern Frontier Preparedness—circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 林之奇

translations.literal: Lin Zhiqi
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zhiqi

sentences.zh: 林之奇，字少穎，福州候官人。

translations.literal: Lin Zhiqi, courtesy name Shaoying, was a native of Houguan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zhiqi, whose courtesy name was Shaoying, came from Houguan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 紫微舍人呂本中入閩，之奇甫冠，從本中學。

translations.literal: When Academician Expositor Lü Benzhong entered Min, Zhiqi had just capped his years and studied with Benzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Academician Expositor Lü Benzhong entered Fujian, Zhiqi had just come of age and studied under him.

sentences.zh: 時將試禮部，行次衢州，以不得事親而反。

translations.literal: At the time he was about to take the civil-service examination for the Ministry of Rites; passing through Quzhou, he turned back because he could not serve his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to take the Ministry of Rites examination but turned back while passing through Quzhou because he could not leave his parents.

sentences.zh: 學益力，本中奇之，由是學者踵至。

translations.literal: His learning grew ever stronger; Benzhong marveled at him, and from this scholars came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: His learning grew stronger still. Benzhong marveled at him, and scholars came in succession.

sentences.zh: 中紹興二十一年進士第，調莆田簿，改尉長汀，召為秘書省正字，轉校書郎。
