translations.literal: He passed the Jinshi degree in the twenty-first year of Shaoxing, was appointed Clerk of Putian, changed to Assistant Magistrate of Changting, and was summoned to be Regular Scribe of the Secretariat, then transferred to Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-first year of Shaoxing, served as clerk of Putian, then as assistant magistrate of Changting, and was summoned as regular scribe of the Secretariat and later proofreader.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷欲令學者參用王安石《三經義》之說，之奇上言：「王氏三經，率為新法地。

translations.literal: When the court wished to have scholars also use Wang Anshi's exegesis of the Three Classics, Zhiqi memorialized: "Wang's three classics are mostly ground for the New Policies.
translations.idiomatic: When the court wished scholars to use Wang Anshi's exegesis of the Three Classics, Zhiqi memorialized, "Wang's three classics served chiefly as ground for the New Policies.

sentences.zh: 晉人以王、何清談之罪，深於桀、紂。

translations.literal: The Jin people held Wang and He of the Pure Conversation guilty of a crime deeper than Jie and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin held Wang and He of the Pure Conversation school guilty of a crime deeper than Jie and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 本朝靖康禍亂，考其端倪，王氏實負王、何之責。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's Jingkang calamity, examining its origins, finds Wang in truth bore the guilt of Wang and He.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the origins of our dynasty's Jingkang calamity, Wang in truth bore the guilt of Wang and He.

sentences.zh: 在孔、孟書，正所謂邪說、詖行、淫辭之不可訓者。」

translations.literal: In the books of Confucius and Mencius, this is precisely what is called heterodox doctrine, perverse conduct, and excessive language that cannot instruct."
translations.idiomatic: In the books of Confucius and Mencius, this is precisely the heterodox doctrine, perverse conduct, and excessive language that cannot instruct."

sentences.zh: 或傳金人欲南侵，之奇作書抵當路，以為「久和畏戰，人情之常。

translations.literal: Rumor spread that the Jurchen wished to invade south; Zhiqi wrote to those in power, holding that "long peace breeds fear of war—this is the constant of human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor spread that the Jurchen wished to invade south. Zhiqi wrote to those in power: "Long peace breeds fear of war—that is human nature.

sentences.zh: 金知吾重於和，故常以虛聲喝我，而示我以欲戰之意，非果欲戰，所以堅吾和。

translations.literal: The Jurchen know we value peace and therefore often use empty threats against us while showing an intent to fight—not truly wishing to fight, but to strengthen our commitment to peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen know we value peace and therefore often threaten us with empty alarms while showing an intent to fight—not because they truly wish to fight, but to strengthen our commitment to peace.

sentences.zh: 欲與之和，宜無憚於戰，則其權在我」。

translations.literal: If one wishes peace with them, one ought not fear war—then the initiative rests with us."
translations.idiomatic: If we wish peace with them, we ought not fear war—then the initiative rests with us."

sentences.zh: 又言：「戰之所須不一，而人才為先。

translations.literal: He also said: "What war requires is not uniform, but talent comes first.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "What war requires is many things, but talent comes first.

sentences.zh: 必求可與共患難者，非得如龐士元所謂俊傑者不可也。」

translations.literal: One must seek those who can share hardship—none but the outstanding men of whom Pang Shiyuan spoke will do."
translations.idiomatic: We must seek those who can share our hardships—none but the outstanding men of whom Pang Shiyuan spoke will suffice."

sentences.zh: 以痹疾乞外，由宗正丞提舉閩舶，參帥議，遂以祠祿家居，自稱拙齋。

translations.literal: He begged to leave office on account of paralysis, was promoted from Director of the Imperial Clan Court to oversee Fujian shipping and take part in commanders' deliberations, then retired on temple stipend at home, styling himself the Clumsy Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave on account of paralysis, was promoted from director of the Imperial Clan Court to oversee Fujian shipping and join commanders' deliberations, then retired on temple stipend at home under the name Clumsy Studio.

sentences.zh: 東萊呂祖謙嘗受學焉。

translations.literal: Lü Zuqian of Donglai once received instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuqian of Donglai once studied under him.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年卒，年六十有五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunxi he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Chunxi at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 有《書》《春秋》《周禮說》、《論》、《孟》《楊子講義》、《道山記聞》等書行於世。

translations.literal: His writings include exegeses of the Documents, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Rites of Zhou, Lectures on the Analects, Mencius, and Yangzi, and Records Heard on the Dao Mountain, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works—including exegeses of the Documents, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Rites of Zhou, lectures on the Analects, Mencius, and Yangzi, and Records Heard on the Dao Mountain—circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 林光朝

translations.literal: Lin Guangchao
translations.idiomatic: Lin Guangchao

sentences.zh: 林光朝，字謙之，興化軍莆田人。

translations.literal: Lin Guangchao, courtesy name Qianzhi, was a native of Putian in the Xinghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Guangchao, whose courtesy name was Qianzhi, came from Putian in the Xinghua circuit.

sentences.zh: 再試禮部不第，聞吳中陸子正嘗從尹焞學，因往從之遊。

translations.literal: He twice took the Ministry of Rites examination without passing; hearing that Lu Zizheng in Wu had studied with Yin Chun, he went to study with him.
translations.idiomatic: He twice failed the Ministry of Rites examination. Hearing that Lu Zizheng in Wu had studied with Yin Chun, he went to study with him.

sentences.zh: 自是專心聖賢踐履之學，通《六經》，貫百氏，言動必以禮，四方來學者亡慮數百人。

translations.literal: From this he devoted himself to the learning of practicing the sages and worthies, mastered the Six Classics, penetrated the hundred schools, and in speech and conduct always kept to ritual—scholars who came from the four directions numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he devoted himself to practicing the way of the sages, mastered the Six Classics, penetrated the hundred schools, and in speech and conduct always kept to ritual. Scholars came from all directions by the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，以伊、洛之學倡東南者，自光朝始。

translations.literal: After the southward move, in advocating the learning of the Yi and Luo schools in the southeast, Guangchao was the first.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward move, Guangchao was the first to advocate the Yi and Luo learning in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 然未嘗著書，惟口授學者，使之心通理解。

translations.literal: Yet he never wrote books; he only orally instructed scholars, making them understand with the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he never wrote books. He instructed scholars orally until they understood with the heart.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「道之全體，全乎太虛。

translations.literal: He once said: "The full body of the Way is complete in the Great Void.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "The full body of the Way is complete in the Great Void.

sentences.zh: 《六經》既發明之，後世注解固已支離，若復增加，道愈遠矣。」

translations.literal: The Six Classics have already elucidated it; later exegeses were already fragmented, and if one adds more, the Way grows ever farther."
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics have already elucidated it. Later exegeses were already fragmented; if one adds more, the Way grows ever farther."

sentences.zh: 孝宗隆興元年，光朝年五十，以進士及第。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing of Xiaozong, Guangchao was fifty and passed the Jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing, Guangchao was fifty and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調袁州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Clerk for Revenue in Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed clerk for revenue in Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道三年，龍大淵、曾覿以潛邸恩幸進，台諫、給舍論駁不行。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiandao, Long Dayuan and Zeng Di advanced on favor from the hidden residence; the censorate, remonstrators, and drafters debated and blocked it without effect.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiandao, Long Dayuan and Zeng Di advanced through favor from the hidden residence. Censors, remonstrators, and drafters debated and blocked them without effect.

sentences.zh: 張闡自外召為執政，銳欲去之，覺其不可拙，遂以老疾力辭不拜。

translations.literal: Zhang Kan was summoned from outside to be chief minister and keenly wished to remove them; perceiving it could not be done clumsily, he pleaded old age and illness and strenuously declined appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kan was summoned from outside as chief minister and keenly wished to remove them. Perceiving this could not be done clumsily, he pleaded old age and illness and declined appointment.

sentences.zh: 而光朝及劉朔方以名儒薦對，頗及二人罪，由是光朝改左承奉郎、知永福縣。

translations.literal: Guangchao and Liu Shuo were recommended as famous Confucians for audience and spoke at length of the crimes of the two men; thereupon Guangchao was changed to Left Gentleman for Court Service and made Prefect of Yongfu County.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchao and Liu Shuo were recommended as famous Confucians for audience and spoke at length of the two men's crimes. Guangchao was then changed to Left Gentleman for Court Service and made prefect of Yongfu County.

sentences.zh: 而大臣論薦不已，召試館職，為秘書省正字兼國史編修、實錄檢討官，曆著作佐郎兼禮部郎官。

translations.literal: Yet the great ministers' recommendations did not cease; he was summoned to test for a library post, made Regular Scribe of the Secretariat with concurrent compilation of the national history and collation of the veritable records, and served successively as Assistant Compiler with concurrent Rites Office official.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the great ministers kept recommending him. He was summoned to test for a library post, made regular scribe with concurrent duty compiling the national history and collating the veritable records, and served as assistant compiler with concurrent rites office official.

sentences.zh: 八年，進國子司業兼太子侍讀，史職如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education with concurrent Reader for the Heir Apparent, his history duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education with concurrent reader for the heir apparent, his history duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 是時，張說再除簽書樞密院事，光朝不往賀，遂出為廣西提點刑獄，移廣東。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yue was again appointed to sign documents in the Bureau of Military Affairs; Guangchao did not go to congratulate him and was sent out to be Judicial Commissioner of Guangxi, then transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yue was again appointed to sign documents in the Bureau of Military Affairs. Guangchao did not congratulate him and was sent out as judicial commissioner of Guangxi, then transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 茶寇自荊、湘剽江西，薄嶺南，其鋒銳甚。

translations.literal: Tea bandits from Jing and Xiang plundered Jiangxi and pressed toward Lingnan; their edge was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Tea bandits from Jing and Xiang plundered Jiangxi and pressed toward Lingnan with a very sharp edge.

sentences.zh: 光朝自將郡兵，檄摧鋒統製路海、本路鈐轄黃進各以軍分控要害。

translations.literal: Guangchao himself led the prefectural troops and ordered Crushing Edge Overall Commander Lu Hai and the circuit commander Huang Jin each to control strategic points with their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchao himself led the prefectural troops and ordered Crushing Edge Overall Commander Lu Hai and circuit commander Huang Jin each to hold strategic points with their armies.

sentences.zh: 會有詔徙光朝轉運副使，光朝謂賊勢方張，留屯不去，督二將遮擊，連敗之，賊驚懼宵遁。

translations.literal: When an edict arrived transferring Guangchao to Vice Transport Commissioner, Guangchao said the bandits' momentum was still strong, remained encamped without leaving, supervised the two generals in intercepting attacks, defeated them repeatedly, and the bandits fled in fear by night.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict arrived transferring him to vice transport commissioner, Guangchao said the bandits' momentum was still strong, remained without leaving, supervised the two generals in intercepting attacks, defeated them repeatedly, and the bandits fled by night in fear.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，喜曰：「林光朝儒生，乃知兵耶。」

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of it and rejoiced: "Lin Guangchao is a Confucian scholar—yet he knows warfare!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it and rejoiced: "Lin Guangchao is a Confucian scholar—yet he knows warfare!"

sentences.zh: 加直寶謨閣，召拜國子祭酒兼太子左諭德。

translations.literal: He was given the title of Direct Academician Expositor and summoned as Libationer of the Directorate of Education with concurrent Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the title Direct Academician Expositor and summoned as libationer with concurrent left tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝幸國子監，命講《中庸》，帝大稱善，麵賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Emperor visited the Imperial University and ordered him to lecture on the Doctrine of the Mean; the Emperor greatly praised it and granted him gold and purple in audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the emperor visited the Imperial University and ordered him to lecture on the Doctrine of the Mean. The emperor greatly praised it and granted him gold and purple in audience.

sentences.zh: 不數日，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: Within a few days he was appointed Drafting Academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days he was appointed drafting academician of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時，吏部郎謝廓然由曾覿薦，賜出身，除殿中侍御史，命從中出。

translations.literal: At that time Xie Kuoran of the Ministry of Personnel was recommended by Zeng Di, granted office by favor, and appointed Palace Attendant Censor—the order came from the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xie Kuoran of the Ministry of Personnel was recommended by Zeng Di, granted office by favor, and appointed palace attendant censor by order from the inner court.

sentences.zh: 光朝愕曰：「是輕台諫、羞科目也。」

translations.literal: Guangchao was startled and said: "This belittles the censorate and shames the examination system."
translations.idiomatic: Guangchao was startled and said, "This belittles the censorate and shames the examination system."

sentences.zh: 立封還詞頭。

translations.literal: He immediately sealed and returned the draft.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sealed and returned the draft.

sentences.zh: 天子度光朝決不奉詔，改授工部侍郎，不拜，遂以集英殿修撰出知婺州。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven gauged that Guangchao would certainly not accept the order, changed the appointment to Vice Minister of Works, but he did not accept and was sent out as Compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence to be Prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gauged that Guangchao would not accept the order, changed the appointment to vice minister of works, but he did not accept and was sent out as compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence to be prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 光朝老儒，素有士望。

translations.literal: Guangchao was an elder Confucian who had long enjoyed scholarly repute.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchao was an elder Confucian who had long enjoyed scholarly repute.

sentences.zh: 在後省未有建明，或疑之，及聞繳駁廓然，士論始服。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat he had made no great proposals, and some doubted him; when they heard he had returned Kuoran's draft, scholarly opinion at last approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat he had made no great proposals, and some doubted him. When they heard he had returned Kuoran's draft, scholarly opinion at last approved.

sentences.zh: 光朝因引疾提舉興國宮，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: Guangchao thereupon cited illness and was put in charge of the Xingguo Abbey; he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchao thereupon cited illness, was put in charge of the Xingguo Abbey, and died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 楊萬里

translations.literal: Yang Wanli
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wanli

sentences.zh: 楊萬里，字廷秀，吉州吉水人。

translations.literal: Yang Wanli, courtesy name Tingxiu, was a native of Jishui in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wanli, whose courtesy name was Tingxiu, came from Jishui in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 中紹興二十四年進士第，為贛州司戶，調永州零陵丞。

translations.literal: He passed the Jinshi degree in the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing, served as Clerk for Revenue in Ganzhou, and was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Lingling in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing, served as clerk for revenue in Ganzhou, and was transferred to assistant magistrate of Lingling in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時張浚謫永，杜門謝客，萬里三往不得見，以書力請，始見之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Jun was banished to Yong, closed his gate and refused visitors; Wanli went three times without seeing him, wrote forcefully begging an audience, and at last saw him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Jun was banished to Yong and closed his gate to visitors. Wanli went three times without seeing him, wrote forcefully begging an audience, and at last was received.

sentences.zh: 浚勉以正心誠意之學，萬里服其教終身，乃名讀書之室曰誠齋。

translations.literal: Jun exhorted him with the learning of rectifying the mind and making the will sincere; Wanli submitted to his teaching for life and named his study the Sincerity Studio.
translations.idiomatic: Jun exhorted him with the learning of rectifying the mind and making the will sincere. Wanli submitted to his teaching for life and named his study the Sincerity Studio.

sentences.zh: 浚入相，薦之朝。

translations.literal: When Jun entered the chancellorship he recommended Wanli to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun became chief minister he recommended Wanli to court.

sentences.zh: 除臨安府教授，未赴，丁父憂。

translations.literal: He was appointed Professor of Lin'an Prefecture but had not yet reported when he mourned his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor of Lin'an Prefecture but had not yet reported when his father died.

sentences.zh: 改知隆興府奉新縣，戢追胥不入鄉，民逋賦者揭其名市中，民讙趨之，賦不擾而足，縣以大治，會陳俊卿、虞允文為相，交薦之，召為國子博士。

translations.literal: He was changed to be Prefect of Fengxin County in Longxing Prefecture, restrained the pursuing clerks from entering the villages, and for those who owed taxes posted their names in the market—the people gladly hurried to pay, taxes were not disturbed yet were sufficient, and the county was greatly well governed. When Chen Junqing and Yu Yunwen were chief ministers they jointly recommended him and he was summoned to be Doctor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Fengxin County in Longxing Prefecture, kept tax pursuers out of the villages, and posted the names of tax delinquents in the market. The people gladly paid, taxes were collected without disturbance, and the county was greatly well governed. When Chen Junqing and Yu Yunwen were chief ministers they jointly recommended him, and he was summoned as doctor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 侍講張栻以論張說出守袁，萬里抗疏留栻，又遺允文書，以和同之說規之，栻雖不果留，而公論偉之。

translations.literal: Lecturer Zhang Shi, on debating Zhang Yue, went out to guard Yuan; Wanli memorialized strenuously to retain Shi and also wrote Yunwen a letter admonishing him with the doctrine of harmony—Shi though not retained, yet public opinion praised Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturer Zhang Shi, after debating Zhang Yue, went out to guard Yuan. Wanli memorialized strenuously to retain Shi and wrote Yunwen admonishing him with the doctrine of harmony. Though Shi was not retained, public opinion praised Wanli.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，尋升丞兼吏部侍右郎官，轉將作少監、出知漳州，改常州，尋提舉廣東常平茶鹽。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, soon promoted to Vice Director with concurrent official of the Ministry of Personnel's right section, then Director of Works and sent out to be Prefect of Zhangzhou, changed to Changzhou, and soon promoted to oversee Guangdong grain and salt.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, soon promoted to vice director with concurrent official of the Ministry of Personnel's right section, then director of works and sent out as prefect of Zhangzhou, changed to Changzhou, and soon promoted to oversee Guangdong grain and salt.

sentences.zh: 盜沈師犯南粵，帥師往平之。

translations.literal: The bandit Shen Shi invaded southern Yue; Wanli led troops and went to pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Shen Shi invaded southern Yue. Wanli led troops to pacify him.

sentences.zh: 孝宗稱之曰「仁者之勇」，遂有大用意，就除提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Xiaozong praised him as "the courage of the humane" and thereupon had great intent to employ him; he was thereupon appointed Judicial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong praised him as "the courage of the humane" and thereupon intended to employ him greatly; he was appointed judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 請於潮、惠二州築外砦，潮以鎮賊之巢，惠以扼賊之路。

translations.literal: He requested outer fortresses at Chao and Hui prefectures—Chao to pin the bandits' nest, Hui to block the bandits' route.
translations.idiomatic: He requested outer fortresses at Chao and Hui—Chao to pin the bandits' nest, Hui to block their route.

sentences.zh: 俄以憂去。

translations.literal: Before long he left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he left on account of mourning.

sentences.zh: 免喪，召為尚左郎官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned to be Left Official of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned as left official of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十二年五月，以地震，應詔上書曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twelfth year of Chunxi, on account of an earthquake, by imperial order he memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twelfth year of Chunxi, on account of an earthquake, by imperial order he memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞：言有事於無事之時，不害其為忠；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: to speak of affairs when there are no affairs does not harm one's loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard: to speak of danger when there is no danger does not harm one's loyalty;

sentences.zh: 言無事於有事之時，其為奸也大矣。

translations.literal: to speak of no affairs when there are affairs—its treachery is great.
translations.idiomatic: to speak of safety when there is danger—its treachery is great.

sentences.zh: 南北和好逾二十年，一旦絕使，敵情不測。

translations.literal: North and south have been at peace more than twenty years; suddenly envoys are cut off and the enemy's intent cannot be gauged.
translations.idiomatic: North and south have been at peace more than twenty years. Suddenly envoys are cut off and the enemy's intent cannot be gauged.

sentences.zh: 而或者曰：彼有五單于爭立之禍。

translations.literal: Yet some say: they have the calamity of five Shanyu contending for rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some say they have the calamity of five Shanyu contending for rule.

sentences.zh: 又曰：彼有匈奴困於東胡之禍，既而皆不驗。

translations.literal: Others say: they have the calamity of the Xiongnu trapped by the Eastern Hu—yet in time neither proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Others say they have the calamity of the Xiongnu trapped by the Eastern Hu—yet in time neither proved true.

sentences.zh: 道塗相傳，繕汴京城池，開海州漕渠，又於河南、北簽民兵，增驛騎，製馬櫪，籍井泉，而吾之間諜不得以入，此何為者耶？

translations.literal: Travelers on the road report repairs to the walls of Bianjing, opening the transport canal at Haizhou, and also conscripting militia north and south of the Yellow River, increasing post horses, making horse mangers, registering wells and springs—yet our spies cannot enter. What is all this for?
translations.idiomatic: Travelers report repairs to the walls of Bianjing, opening the transport canal at Haizhou, conscripting militia north and south of the Yellow River, increasing post horses, making horse mangers, and registering wells and springs—yet our spies cannot enter. What is all this for?

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者一也。

translations.literal: Your servant's first instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 或謂金主北歸，可為中國之賀。

translations.literal: Some say that the Jin ruler's return to the north may be celebrated for China.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the Jin ruler's return to the north is cause for China to rejoice.

sentences.zh: 臣以中國之憂，正在乎此。

translations.literal: Your servant takes China's worry to lie precisely in this.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that China's worry lies precisely in this.

sentences.zh: 此人北歸，蓋懲創於逆亮之空國而南侵也。

translations.literal: This man's return to the north is likely chastened by Prince Hailing's emptying the state to invade south.
translations.idiomatic: This ruler's return north was likely chastened by Prince Hailing's emptying the state to invade the south.

sentences.zh: 將欲南之，必固北之。

translations.literal: If one intends to go south, one must first secure the north.
translations.idiomatic: To advance south, one must first secure the north.

sentences.zh: 或者以身填撫其北，而以其子與婿經營其南也。

translations.literal: Perhaps with his own person he pacifies the north, while with his sons and sons-in-law he manages the south.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps he himself pacifies the north in person, while deploying his sons and sons-in-law to manage the south.

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者二也。

translations.literal: Your servant's second instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 臣竊聞論者或謂緩急，淮不可守，則棄淮而守江，是大不然。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately heard debaters say that in crisis, if the Huai cannot be held, then abandon the Huai and guard the Yangzi—a great error.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard some argue that in a crisis, if the Huai cannot be held, we should abandon it and defend the Yangzi. This is gravely mistaken.

sentences.zh: 昔者吳與魏力爭而得合肥，然後吳始安。

translations.literal: Formerly Wu contested with Wei strenuously and obtained Hefei—only then did Wu begin to be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Wu struggled with Wei and secured Hefei; only then did Wu become secure.

sentences.zh: 李煜失滁、揚二州，自此南唐始蹙。

translations.literal: When Li Yu lost Chuzhou and Yangzhou, from then South Tang began to be compressed.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu lost Chuz and Yang, South Tang began to shrink from that point on.

sentences.zh: 今曰棄淮而保江，既無淮矣，江可得而保乎？

translations.literal: Now to say abandon the Huai and preserve the Yangzi—once there is no Huai, can the Yangzi be preserved?
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon the Huai to preserve the Yangzi, once the Huai is lost, can the Yangzi truly be defended?

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者三也。

translations.literal: Your servant's third instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 今淮東、西凡十五郡，所謂守帥，不知陛下使宰相擇之乎，使樞廷擇之乎？

translations.literal: Now east and west of the Huai there are fifteen commanderies in all—the so-called garrison commanders: does Your Majesty have the chief ministers choose them, or have the Bureau of Military Affairs choose them?
translations.idiomatic: East and west of the Huai there are fifteen commanderies in all. As for their garrison commanders, does Your Majesty have the chief ministers choose them, or the Bureau of Military Affairs?

sentences.zh: 使宰相擇之，宰相未必為樞廷慮也；

translations.literal: If the chief ministers choose them, the chief ministers need not necessarily consider the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: If the chief ministers choose them, they need not necessarily consider the Bureau of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 使樞廷擇之，則除授不自己出也。

translations.literal: if the Bureau of Military Affairs chooses them, then appointments do not issue from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: if the Bureau of Military Affairs chooses them, then appointments do not issue from one's own authority.

sentences.zh: 一則不為之慮，一則不自己出，緩急敗事，則皆曰：非我也。

translations.literal: One side does not consider it; one side does not issue from oneself—in crisis when affairs fail, all will say: 'It was not I.'
translations.idiomatic: One side fails to plan for it; the other fails to take responsibility—in a crisis, when things go wrong, everyone will say, "It was not I."

sentences.zh: 陛下將責之誰乎？

translations.literal: Upon whom will Your Majesty fix blame?
translations.idiomatic: Upon whom will Your Majesty fix blame?

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者四也。

translations.literal: Your servant's fourth instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 且南北各有長技，若騎若射，北之長技也；

translations.literal: Moreover north and south each has strengths: riding and archery are the north's strengths;
translations.idiomatic: North and south each have their strengths: cavalry and archery are the north's;

sentences.zh: 若舟若步，南之長技也。

translations.literal: naval craft and infantry are the south's strengths.
translations.idiomatic: warships and infantry are the south's.

sentences.zh: 今為北之計者，日繕治其海舟，而南之海舟則不聞繕治焉。

translations.literal: Now those planning for the north daily repair their sea vessels, while of the south's sea vessels one hears nothing of repair.
translations.idiomatic: Those planning for the north repair their sea vessels daily, yet one hears nothing of the south doing the same.

sentences.zh: 或曰：吾舟素具也，或曰：舟雖未具而憚於擾也。

translations.literal: Some say: our vessels are already prepared. Others say: though vessels are not yet prepared, one fears disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Some say our fleet is already ready. Others say that though it is not ready, they fear the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 紹興辛巳之戰，山東、采石之功，不以騎也，不以射也，不以步也，舟焉而已。

translations.literal: The battle in xinsi year of Shaoxing—the achievements at Shandong and Caishi owed nothing to cavalry, nothing to archery, nothing to infantry; only to vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi-year battle of Shaoxing, the victories at Shandong and Caishi owed nothing to cavalry, archery, or infantry—only to ships.

sentences.zh: 當時之舟，今可復用乎？

translations.literal: Can the vessels of that time be used again now?
translations.idiomatic: Can the ships of that day be used again now?

sentences.zh: 且夫斯民一日之擾，與社稷百世之安危，孰輕孰重？

translations.literal: Moreover, one day's disturbance for this people, versus the security of state and altars for a hundred generations—which is lighter, which heavier?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, one day's hardship for the people versus the security of the state for a hundred generations—which weighs more?

sentences.zh: 事固有大於擾者也。

translations.literal: There are indeed affairs greater than disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: There are matters more important than temporary hardship.

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者五也。

translations.literal: Your servant's fifth instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 陛下以今日為何等時耶？

translations.literal: What sort of time does Your Majesty take today to be?
translations.idiomatic: What sort of time does Your Majesty take today to be?

sentences.zh: 金人日逼，疆場日擾，而未聞防金人者何策，保疆場者何道？

translations.literal: The Jurchen press daily; the borders are disturbed daily—yet one hears no strategy for guarding against the Jurchen, no method for protecting the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen press closer each day; the frontier grows more troubled each day—yet one hears no strategy for guarding against them, no plan for securing the borders.

sentences.zh: 但聞某日修某禮文也，某日進某書史也，是以鄉飲理軍，以幹羽解圍也。

translations.literal: One only hears that on such a day such ritual texts were revised, on such a day such books and histories were submitted—this is using village drinking rites to manage the army, using dance feathers to break a siege.
translations.idiomatic: One only hears that on such a day such ritual texts were revised, on such a day such books and histories were submitted—as though village drinking rites could discipline an army, or dance feathers could lift a siege.

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者六也。

translations.literal: Your servant's sixth instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古者人君，人不能悟之，則天地能悟之。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in antiquity, when a ruler could not be awakened by men, Heaven and Earth could awaken him.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that in antiquity, when a ruler could not be awakened by men, Heaven and Earth could awaken him.

sentences.zh: 今也國家之事，敵情不測如此，而君臣上下處之如太平無事之時，是人不能悟之矣。

translations.literal: Now on state affairs the enemy's intent is so unpredictable, yet sovereign and ministers above and below treat it as a time of great peace with no affairs—men cannot awaken him.
translations.idiomatic: Today the enemy's intent is so unpredictable, yet sovereign and ministers treat the realm as if it were at peace—men cannot awaken Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 故上天見災異，異時熒惑犯南斗，邇日鎮星犯端門，熒惑守羽林。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven shows portents: at one time Mars trespassed on the Southern Dipper; recently Saturn trespassed on the Gate of Propriety, and Mars holds the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Heaven has sent portents: Mars once trespassed on the Southern Dipper; recently Saturn trespassed on the Gate of Propriety, and Mars holds the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 臣書生，不曉天文，未敢以為必然也。

translations.literal: Your servant is a mere scholar, does not understand astronomy, and dares not take these as certain.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is a mere scholar and does not understand astronomy; I dare not treat these as certain.

sentences.zh: 至於春正月日青無光，若有兩日相摩者，茲不曰大異乎？

translations.literal: As for the first month of spring when the sun was dim and greenish, as though two suns were grinding together—is this not called a great portent?
translations.idiomatic: As for the first month of spring, when the sun was dim and greenish, as though two suns were grinding together—is this not a great portent?

sentences.zh: 然天猶恐陛下不信也，至於春日載陽，復有雨雪殺物，茲不曰大異乎？

translations.literal: Yet Heaven still feared Your Majesty would not believe; when spring should bring warmth, again there was snow and rain that killed living things—is this not called a great portent?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven still feared Your Majesty would not believe; when spring should have brought warmth, snow and rain returned and killed living things—is this not a great portent?

sentences.zh: 然天猶恐陛下又不信也，乃五月庚寅，又有地震，茲又不曰大異乎？

translations.literal: Yet Heaven still feared Your Majesty would not believe again; then on gengyin day in the fifth month there was again an earthquake—is this not again called a great portent?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven still feared Your Majesty would not believe; then on gengyin day in the fifth month came another earthquake—is this not again a great portent?

sentences.zh: 且夫天變在遠，臣子不敢奏也，不信可也；

translations.literal: Moreover celestial changes are distant—a subject dares not memorialize; disbelief is possible;
translations.idiomatic: Celestial changes are distant, and subjects dare not report them—disbelief is possible;

sentences.zh: 地震在外，州郡不敢聞也，不信可也。

translations.literal: earthquakes abroad—prefectures and commanderies dare not report; disbelief is possible.
translations.idiomatic: earthquakes in distant provinces go unreported—disbelief is possible.

sentences.zh: 今也天變頻仍，地震輦轂，而君臣不聞警懼，朝廷不聞谘訪，人不能悟之，則天地能悟之。

translations.literal: Now celestial changes come in succession, an earthquake at the imperial capital—yet sovereign and ministers show no alarm, the court hears no consultation. If men cannot awaken him, Heaven and Earth can.
translations.idiomatic: Now portents come one after another, and an earthquake has struck the capital—yet sovereign and ministers show no alarm, and the court holds no consultations. If men cannot awaken Your Majesty, Heaven and Earth can.

sentences.zh: 臣不知陛下於此悟乎，否乎？

translations.literal: Your servant does not know whether Your Majesty is awakened by this or not.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant does not know whether Your Majesty has been awakened by this.

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者七也。

translations.literal: Your servant's seventh instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 自頻年以來，兩浙最近則先旱，江淮則又旱，湖廣則又旱，流徙者相續，道堇相枕。

translations.literal: In successive years in recent times, first Liangzhe droughted earliest; then Jianghuai again droughted; then Huguang again droughted. Displaced persons followed one after another; the roads were lined with dead from famine.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years drought has struck Liangzhe first, then Jianghuai, then Huguang. Refugees have followed one after another, and the roads have been lined with the dead from famine.

sentences.zh: 而常平之積，名存而實亡；

translations.literal: Yet the Ever-Normal granaries—the name exists but the reality is gone;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Ever-Normal granaries exist in name only;

sentences.zh: 入粟之令，上行而下慢。

translations.literal: the order to submit grain goes up but is sluggish below.
translations.idiomatic: orders to submit grain are issued above but implemented slowly below.

sentences.zh: 靜而無事，未知所以振救之；

translations.literal: In quiet with no crisis, one does not yet know how to rescue;
translations.idiomatic: In times of peace we do not yet know how to provide relief;

sentences.zh: 動而有事，將何以仰以為資耶？

translations.literal: if movement brings crisis, on what will one rely for resources?
translations.idiomatic: if crisis comes, what resources will we have to draw upon?

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者八也。

translations.literal: Your servant's eighth instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 古者足國裕民，惟食與貨。

translations.literal: In antiquity to fill the state and enrich the people, there were only grain and currency.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a state was made strong and its people enriched through grain and currency alone.

sentences.zh: 今之所謂錢者，富商、巨賈、閹宦、權貴皆盈室以藏之，至於百姓三軍之用，惟破楮券爾。

translations.literal: Now what is called money—great merchants, massive traders, eunuchs, and powerful nobles all fill their chambers hiding it; as for the people and the three armies' use, there are only worn paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: Today what passes for money is hoarded by great merchants, eunuchs, and powerful nobles until their chambers overflow, while the people and the armies must make do with worn paper notes.

sentences.zh: 萬一如唐涇原之師，因怒糲食，蹴而覆之，出不遜語，遂起朱泚之亂，可不為寒心哉！

translations.literal: If by any chance, like the Jingyuan troops of Tang, enraged at coarse rations, kicked over their food and spoke insolently, giving rise to Zhu Ci's rebellion—can one not shudder?
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance, as with the Jingyuan troops of Tang—enraged at coarse rations, they kicked over their food, spoke insolently, and gave rise to Zhu Ci's rebellion—can we not shudder at the thought?

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者九也。

translations.literal: Your servant's ninth instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ninth of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 古者立國必有可畏，非畏其國也，畏其人也。

translations.literal: In antiquity to establish a state there had to be something formidable—not fear of the state, but fear of its people.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a state had to command respect—not through its territory, but through its people.

sentences.zh: 故苻堅欲圖晉，而王猛以為不可，謂謝安、桓衝江左之望，是存晉者，二人而已。

translations.literal: Therefore when Fu Jian wished to plot against Jin, Wang Meng thought it impossible, saying Xie An and Huan Chong were the hope of the lands east of the Yangzi—those who preserved Jin were these two alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian wished to conquer Jin, Wang Meng thought it impossible, saying Xie An and Huan Chong were the hope of the lands east of the Yangzi—the men who preserved Jin were these two alone.

sentences.zh: 異時名相如趙鼎、張浚，名將如岳飛、韓世忠，此金人所憚也。

translations.literal: In former times chief ministers named Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun, generals named Yue Fei and Han Shizhong—these the Jurchen feared.
translations.idiomatic: In former times chief ministers such as Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun, and generals such as Yue Fei and Han Shizhong—these were the men the Jurchen feared.

sentences.zh: 近時劉珙可用則早死，張栻可用則沮死，萬一有緩急，不知可以督諸軍者何人，可以當一面者何人，而金人之所素憚者又何人？

translations.literal: In recent times Liu Qi was usable but died early; Zhang Shi was usable but died from obstruction. If crisis comes, who can command all armies, who can hold a front alone—and whom do the Jurchen habitually fear?
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Liu Qi was available but died early; Zhang Shi was available but died from obstruction. If crisis comes, who can command all armies, who can hold a front alone—and whom do the Jurchen still fear?

sentences.zh: 而或者謂人之有才，用而後見。

translations.literal: Yet some say talent is seen only after use.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some say a man's talent is known only after he is used.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之《記》曰：「苟有車必見其式，苟有言必聞其聲。」

translations.literal: Your servant has heard in the Record: 'If there is a chariot, one must see its traces; if there is speech, one must hear its sound.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard it said in the Record: "If there is a chariot, one must see its tracks; if there is speech, one must hear its sound."

sentences.zh: 今曰有其人而未聞其可將可相，是有車而無式，有言而無聲也。

translations.literal: Now to say there are such men yet one has not heard who can be general or minister—this is having a chariot without traces, speech without sound.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today we are told such men exist, yet no one is known who can serve as general or minister—this is a chariot without tracks, speech without sound.

sentences.zh: 且夫用而後見，非臨之以大安危，試之以大勝負，則莫見其用也。

translations.literal: Moreover 'seen only after use'—unless confronted with great peril or tested in great victory or defeat, one will not see their use.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if talent is seen only after use, unless tested by great peril or great victory and defeat, one will never see it.

sentences.zh: 平居無以知其人，必待大安危、大勝負而後見焉。

translations.literal: In ordinary times there is no way to know a man; one must wait for great peril or great victory and defeat before seeing.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times there is no way to know a man; one must wait for great peril or great victory and defeat before talent reveals itself.

sentences.zh: 成事幸矣，萬一敗事，悔何及耶？

translations.literal: If affairs succeed, one is fortunate; if by any chance they fail, what regret can match?
translations.idiomatic: If affairs succeed, one is fortunate; if they fail, what regret can compare?

sentences.zh: 昔者謝玄之北禦苻堅，而郗超知其必勝；

translations.literal: Formerly when Xie Xuan defended north against Fu Jian, Xi Chao knew he would surely win;
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Xuan defended the north against Fu Jian, Xi Chao knew he would surely win;

sentences.zh: 桓溫之西伐李勢，而劉倓知其必取。

translations.literal: when Huan Wen marched west against Li Shi, Liu Tan knew he would surely conquer.
translations.idiomatic: when Huan Wen marched west against Li Shi, Liu Tan knew he would surely conquer.

sentences.zh: 蓋玄於履屐之間無不當其任，溫於蒱博不必得則不為，二子於平居無事之日，蓋必有以察其小而後信其大也，豈必大用而後見哉？

translations.literal: Xie Xuan in putting on shoes and clogs was never unfit for his task; Huan Wen in gambling would not act unless he was sure to win—these two in days of ordinary peace must have had means to observe small things before trusting great ones. Must one wait for great employment before seeing?
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan handled even the putting on of shoes with perfect competence; Huan Wen would not gamble unless he was sure to win. Both men, in days of ordinary peace, must have had ways to read small signs before trusting great ones. Must talent wait for great employment before it is seen?

sentences.zh: 臣所謂言有事於無事之時者十也。

translations.literal: Your servant's tenth instance of speaking of affairs when there are no affairs is this.
translations.idiomatic: This is the tenth of what your servant means by speaking of danger when there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 願陛下超然遠覽，昭然遠寤。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty gaze far with detachment and awaken clearly from afar.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty look far with clear detachment and awaken to what lies ahead.

sentences.zh: 勿矜聖德之崇高，而增其所未能；

translations.literal: Do not pride yourself on sagely virtue's loftiness while neglecting what you have not yet achieved;
translations.idiomatic: Do not pride yourself on lofty sagely virtue while neglecting what you have not yet achieved;

sentences.zh: 勿恃中國之生聚，而嚴其所未備。

translations.literal: Do not rely on China's population and wealth while failing to strengthen what is not yet prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Do not rely on China's population and wealth while failing to strengthen what is not yet prepared.

sentences.zh: 勿以天地之變異為適然，而法宣王之懼災；

translations.literal: Do not take Heaven and Earth's portents as mere chance; emulate King Xuan's fear of calamity;
translations.idiomatic: Do not treat Heaven and Earth's portents as mere chance; emulate King Xuan's fear of calamity;

sentences.zh: 勿以臣下之苦言為逆耳，而體太宗之導諫。

translations.literal: Do not take your ministers' bitter words as grating; embody Taizong's way of guiding remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Do not take your ministers' bitter words as grating to the ear; embody Taizong's way of welcoming remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 勿以女謁近習之害政為細故，而監漢、唐季世致亂之由；

translations.literal: Do not take the harm to government from women's access and favored intimates as a minor matter; observe the causes by which Han and Tang late ages fell into chaos;
translations.idiomatic: Do not treat the harm to government from women's access and favored intimates as a minor matter; observe how Han and Tang fell into chaos in their final years;

sentences.zh: 勿以仇讎之包藏為無他，而懲宣、政晚年受禍之酷。

translations.literal: Do not take the enemy's hidden designs as harmless; take warning from the cruel suffering of the late Xuanhe and Zhenghe reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Do not assume the enemy harbors no hidden designs; take warning from the cruel suffering of the late Xuanhe and Zhenghe reigns.

sentences.zh: 責大臣以通知邊事軍務如富弼之請，勿以東西二府異其心；

translations.literal: Charge chief ministers to understand border affairs and military matters as Fu Bi requested; do not let the eastern and western departments diverge in mind;
translations.idiomatic: Charge chief ministers to master border affairs and military matters as Fu Bi urged; do not let the eastern and western departments work at cross purposes;

sentences.zh: 委大臣以薦進謀臣良將如蕭何所奇，勿以文武兩途而殊其轍，勿使賂宦者而得旄節如唐大曆之弊，勿使貨近幸而得招討如梁段凝之敗。

translations.literal: entrust chief ministers to recommend wise counselors and good generals as Xiao He discerned talent; do not treat civil and military paths as separate tracks; do not let bribery to eunuchs win command seals as in the Tang Dalì abuse; do not let purchase of imperial favor win campaign commands as in Liang Duan Ning's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: entrust chief ministers to recommend wise counselors and able generals as Xiao He did; do not treat civil and military service as separate paths; do not let bribery to eunuchs win command seals as in the Tang Dalì abuse; do not let purchase of imperial favor win campaign commands as in Liang Duan Ning's defeat.

sentences.zh: 以重蜀之心而重荊、襄，使東西形勢之相接；

translations.literal: With the same heart that values Shu, value Jing and Xiang, so east and west strategic positions connect;
translations.idiomatic: Value Jing and Xiang as you value Shu, so that east and west strategic positions connect;

sentences.zh: 以保江之心而保兩淮，使表裏唇齒之相依。

translations.literal: With the same heart that protects the Yangzi, protect the two Huai, so outer and inner, lips and teeth, depend on each other.
translations.idiomatic: Defend the two Huai as you defend the Yangzi, so that outer and inner defenses, like lips and teeth, depend on each other.

sentences.zh: 勿以海道為無虞，勿以大江為可恃。

translations.literal: Do not assume the sea routes are safe; do not assume the great river can be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Do not assume the sea routes are secure; do not assume the great river alone can be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 增屯聚糧，治艦扼險。

translations.literal: Increase garrison stores, repair warships, hold critical passes.
translations.idiomatic: Increase garrison stores, repair warships, and hold critical passes.

sentences.zh: 君臣之所谘訪，朝夕之所講求，姑置不急之務，精專備敵之策。

translations.literal: What sovereign and ministers consult and what they pursue morning and night—put aside non-urgent business and concentrate exclusively on strategy against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: What sovereign and ministers discuss and pursue day and night—set aside non-urgent business and concentrate exclusively on preparing against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 庶幾上可消於天變，下不墮於敵奸。

translations.literal: Perhaps then above Heaven's portents may be dispelled, and below you will not fall prey to the enemy's designs.
translations.idiomatic: Then perhaps above Heaven's portents may be dispelled, and below you will not fall prey to the enemy's designs.

sentences.zh: 然天下之事，有本根，有枝葉。

translations.literal: Yet in all under Heaven affairs have root and branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in all affairs under Heaven there are roots and branches.

sentences.zh: 臣前所陳，枝葉而已。

translations.literal: What your servant has stated before are only branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: What your servant has stated before concerns only branches and leaves.

sentences.zh: 所謂本根，則人主不可以自用。

translations.literal: What is called the root is that the ruler must not act on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: What is called the root is that the ruler must not act on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 人主自用，則人臣不任責，然猶未害也。

translations.literal: If the ruler acts on his own authority, ministers do not bear responsibility—yet harm is not yet done.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler acts on his own authority, ministers do not bear responsibility—yet the harm is not yet grave.

sentences.zh: 至於軍事，而猶曰「誰當憂此，吾當自憂」。

translations.literal: But when it comes to military affairs and one still says, 'Who should worry about this? I alone will worry'—
translations.idiomatic: But when it comes to military affairs and one still says, "Who should worry about this? I alone will worry"—

sentences.zh: 今日之事，將無類此？

translations.literal: Will today's affairs not be of this sort?
translations.idiomatic: Will today's affairs not be of this sort?

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「木水有本原。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: 'Wood and water have roots and sources.'
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "Wood and water have roots and sources."

sentences.zh: 聖學高明，願益思其所以本原者。

translations.literal: Your sacred learning is lofty and bright; may you further ponder what the root and source are.
translations.idiomatic: Your sacred learning is lofty and bright; may you further ponder what the root and source are.

sentences.zh: 東宮講官闕，帝親擢萬里為侍讀。

translations.literal: A vacancy opened among the Eastern Palace lecturers; the Emperor personally elevated Wanli to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: A vacancy opened among the Eastern Palace lecturers, and the Emperor personally elevated Wanli to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 宮僚以得端人相賀。

translations.literal: Palace staff congratulated one another on gaining an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: Palace staff congratulated one another on gaining an upright man.

sentences.zh: 他日讀《陸宣公奏議》等書，皆隨事規警，太子深敬之。

translations.literal: Another day reading memorials of Lu Zhi and such books, on each matter he admonished as occasion arose; the Crown Prince deeply respected him.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, while reading the memorials of Lu Zhi and similar works, he admonished the Crown Prince on each matter as occasion arose, and the Crown Prince deeply respected him.

sentences.zh: 王淮為相，一日問曰：「宰相先務者何事？」

translations.literal: When Wang Huai was chief minister, one day he asked: 'What should a chief minister take first as his task?'
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Huai was chief minister, one day he asked: "What should a chief minister take first as his task?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「人才。」

translations.literal: He replied: 'Talent.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Talent."

sentences.zh: 又問：「孰為才？」

translations.literal: He asked again: 'Who are talented?'
translations.idiomatic: He asked again: "Who is talented?"

sentences.zh: 即疏朱熹、袁樞以下六十人以獻，淮次第擢用之。

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized Zhu Xi, Yuan Shu, and sixty others below them as a list; Huai promoted them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a list of Zhu Xi, Yuan Shu, and sixty others below them; Huai promoted them in turn.

sentences.zh: 曆樞密院檢詳，守右司郎中，遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: He passed through inspector at the Bureau of Military Affairs, served as Right Section Director, and was transferred to Left Section Director.
translations.idiomatic: He served as inspector at the Bureau of Military Affairs, then as right section director, and was transferred to left section director.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏旱，萬里復應詔，言：「旱及兩月，然後求言，不曰遲乎？

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year summer drought; Wanli again responded to imperial summons, saying: 'The drought has lasted two months—only then are opinions sought. Is this not late?
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, during a summer drought, Wanli again responded to an imperial summons for memorials, saying: "The drought has lasted two months—only now are opinions sought. Is this not late?

sentences.zh: 上自侍從，下止館職，不曰隘乎？

translations.literal: From attendants above to secretarial posts below—is the circle not too narrow?
translations.idiomatic: From attendants-in-waiting above to secretarial posts below—is the circle not too narrow?

sentences.zh: 今之所以旱者，以上澤不下流，下情不上達，故天地之氣隔絕而不通。」

translations.literal: The reason for drought today is that the upper moisture does not flow down and lower sentiment does not rise up—therefore the qi of Heaven and Earth is blocked and does not pass through."
translations.idiomatic: The drought today comes from upper moisture failing to descend and lower sentiment failing to rise—Heaven and Earth's qi is blocked and cannot pass through."

sentences.zh: 因疏四事以獻，言皆懇切。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized four matters in detail; his words were all earnest.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized four matters in detail, all expressed with earnest conviction.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會高宗崩，孝宗欲行三年喪，創議事堂，命皇太子參決庶務。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, Xiaozong wished to observe three years of mourning, established the Deliberation Hall, and ordered the Crown Prince to decide routine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Xiaozong wished to observe three years of mourning, established the Deliberation Hall, and ordered the crown prince to decide routine affairs.

sentences.zh: 萬里上疏力諫，且上太子書，言：「天無二日，民無二王。

translations.literal: Wanli memorialized strenuously in opposition and also submitted a letter to the heir apparent, saying: "Heaven has not two suns; the people have not two kings.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli memorialized strenuously in opposition and wrote the heir apparent: "Heaven has not two suns; the people have not two kings.

sentences.zh: 一履危機，悔之何及？

translations.literal: Once you tread crisis, regret will be too late!
translations.idiomatic: Once you tread crisis, regret will be too late!

sentences.zh: 與其悔之而無及，孰若辭之而不居。

translations.literal: Rather than regret when it is too late, better to decline and not occupy the position.
translations.idiomatic: Better to decline now than regret when it is too late.

sentences.zh: 願殿下三辭五辭，而必不居也。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Highness to decline three times, five times, and by all means not occupy it."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to decline three times, five times, and refuse the post entirely."

sentences.zh: 太子悚然。

translations.literal: The heir apparent was startled.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent was startled.

sentences.zh: 高宗未葬，翰林學士洪邁不俟集議，配饗獨以呂頤浩等姓名上。

translations.literal: Before Gaozong was buried, Academician Hong Mai, without awaiting collective deliberation, submitted for sacrificial companionship only the names of Lü Yihao and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before Gaozong was buried, Academician Hong Mai, without awaiting collective deliberation, submitted for sacrificial companionship only the names of Lü Yihao and others.

sentences.zh: 萬里上疏詆之，力言張浚當預，且謂邁無異指鹿為馬。

translations.literal: Wanli memorialized to denounce this, arguing strenuously that Zhang Jun ought to be included, and said Mai was no different from calling a deer a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli memorialized denouncing this, arguing that Zhang Jun ought to be included, and said Mai was no different from calling a deer a horse.

sentences.zh: 孝宗覽疏不悅，曰：「萬里以朕為何如主！」

translations.literal: Xiaozong read the memorial and was displeased, saying: "What kind of ruler does Wanli take me for!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong read the memorial displeased and said, "What kind of ruler does Wanli take me for!"

sentences.zh: 由是以直秘閣出知筠州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as Direct Academician Expositor to be Prefect of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Direct Academician Expositor to serve as prefect of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，召為秘書監。

translations.literal: When Guangzong acceded, Wanli was summoned to be Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong acceded, Wanli was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「天下有無形之禍，僭非權臣而僭於權臣，擾非盜賊而擾於盜賊，其惟朋黨之論乎！

translations.literal: In audience he said: "The realm has formless calamities—usurpation not by powerful ministers but usurpation by powerful ministers' power; disturbance not by bandits but disturbance by bandits' power—these are none other than factional doctrines!
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said, "The realm has formless calamities—usurpation not by powerful ministers but by their power; disturbance not by bandits but by bandits' power—none other than factional doctrines!

sentences.zh: 蓋欲激人主之怒莫如朋黨，空天下人才莫如朋黨。

translations.literal: To stir the sovereign's anger nothing surpasses factions; to empty the realm's talent nothing surpasses factions.
translations.idiomatic: To stir the sovereign's anger nothing surpasses factions; to empty the realm's talent nothing surpasses factions.

sentences.zh: 黨論一興，其端發於士大夫，其禍及於天下。

translations.literal: Once factional doctrine rises, it begins among court gentlemen and its calamity reaches the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Once factional doctrine rises, it begins among court gentlemen and its calamity reaches the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 前事已然，願陛下建皇極於聖心，公聽並觀，壞植散群，曰君子從而用之，曰小人從而廢之，皆勿問其某黨某黨也。」

translations.literal: The precedent is already clear. I beg Your Majesty establish the supreme pole in the sacred heart, listen publicly and observe together, break up cliques and scatter groups, saying of gentlemen—employ them; of petty men—dismiss them—and ask not which faction they belong to."
translations.idiomatic: The precedent is clear. I beg Your Majesty establish the supreme pole in your sacred heart, listen publicly and observe together, break up cliques, say of gentlemen—employ them, of petty men—dismiss them—and ask not which faction they belong to."

sentences.zh: 又論：「古之帝王，固有以知一己攬其權，不知臣下竊其權。

translations.literal: He also discussed: "Ancient emperors and kings indeed knew how to grasp power themselves yet did not know that subordinates stole their power.
translations.idiomatic: He also discussed how ancient emperors grasped power themselves yet did not know subordinates stole it.

sentences.zh: 大臣竊之則權在大臣，大將竊之則權在大將，外戚竊之則權在外戚，近習竊之則權在近習。

translations.literal: When great ministers steal it, power lies with great ministers; when great generals steal it, power lies with great generals; when maternal kin steal it, power lies with maternal kin; when close attendants steal it, power lies with close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers steal it, power lies with ministers; when generals steal it, with generals; when maternal kin steal it, with maternal kin; when close attendants steal it, with attendants.

sentences.zh: 竊權之最難防者，其惟近習乎！

translations.literal: Of stolen power the hardest to guard against is close attendants!
translations.idiomatic: Of stolen power the hardest to guard against is close attendants!

sentences.zh: 非敢公竊也，私竊之也。

translations.literal: They dare not steal it openly—they steal it privately.
translations.idiomatic: They dare not steal openly—they steal privately.

sentences.zh: 始於私竊，其終必至於公竊而後已。

translations.literal: Beginning with private theft, in the end they necessarily reach open theft before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning with private theft, they necessarily end in open theft.

sentences.zh: 可不懼哉！」

translations.literal: Can one not fear this!"
translations.idiomatic: Can one not fear this!"

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，借煥章閣學士為接伴金國賀正旦使兼實錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he was lent as Academician Expositor of the Huanzhang Hall to serve as reception commissioner for the Jin state's New Year's envoy with concurrent collation duty in the Veritable Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi he was lent as Academician Expositor of the Huanzhang Hall to receive the Jin New Year's envoy, with concurrent collation duty in the Veritable Records Office.

sentences.zh: 會《孝宗日曆》成，參知政事王藺以故事俾萬里序之，而宰臣屬之禮部郎官傅伯壽。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Daily Record was completed, Vice Minister Wang Lin by precedent had Wanli write the preface, but the chief ministers assigned it to Rites Office official Fu Boshou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiaozong Daily Record was completed, Vice Minister Wang Lin by precedent assigned Wanli the preface, but the chief ministers gave it to Rites Office official Fu Boshou.

sentences.zh: 萬里以失職力丐去，帝宣諭勉留。

translations.literal: Wanli, having lost his duty, strenuously begged to leave; the Emperor announced encouragement for him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli, having lost the assignment, strenuously begged to leave; the emperor encouraged him to remain.

sentences.zh: 會進《孝宗聖政》，萬里當奉進，孝宗猶不悅，遂出為江東轉運副使，權總領淮西、江東軍馬錢糧。

translations.literal: When presenting the Xiaozong Sagely Governance, Wanli was to present it; Xiaozong was still displeased, and Wanli was sent out as Vice Transport Commissioner of Jiangdong with authority over funds and grain for Huai-West and Jiangdong armies.
translations.idiomatic: When presenting the Xiaozong Sagely Governance, Wanli was to present it. Xiaozong remained displeased and sent him out as vice transport commissioner of Jiangdong with authority over funds and grain for Huai-West and Jiangdong armies.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲行鐵錢於江南諸郡，萬里疏其不便，不奉詔，忤宰相意，改知贛州，不赴，乞祠，除秘閣修撰，提舉萬壽宮，自是不復出矣。

translations.literal: Court deliberation wished to circulate iron cash in the Jiangnan prefectures; Wanli memorialized its inconvenience, did not obey the edict, offended the chief minister, was changed to be Prefect of Ganzhou, did not go, begged temple service, was made Honorary Compiler of the Secretariat and put in charge of the Wanshou Palace—from this he never went out again.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to circulate iron cash in Jiangnan prefectures. Wanli memorialized against it, disobeyed the edict, offended the chief minister, was appointed prefect of Ganzhou but did not go, begged temple service, was made honorary compiler overseeing the Wanshou Palace, and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 寧宗嗣位，召赴行在，辭。

translations.literal: When Ningzong acceded, Wanli was summoned to the traveling palace and declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong acceded, Wanli was summoned to court and declined.

sentences.zh: 升煥章閣待制、提舉興國宮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Academician Expositor of the Huanzhang Hall and put in charge of the Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Academician Expositor of the Huanzhang Hall and put in charge of the Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 引年乞休致，進寶文閣待制致仕。

translations.literal: He cited old age and begged retirement; he was promoted to Attendant Academician Expositor of the Baowen Hall and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He cited old age and retired with the title Attendant Academician Expositor of the Baowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年，詔進寶謨閣直學士，給賜衣帶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiatai an edict promoted him to Direct Academician Expositor of the Baomo Hall and granted robes and belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiatai an edict promoted him to Direct Academician Expositor of the Baomo Hall and granted robes and belt.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年召，復辭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi he was summoned and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaixi he was summoned and again declined.

sentences.zh: 明年，升寶謨閣學士，卒，年八十三，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Academician Expositor of the Baomo Hall, died, aged eighty-three, and was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Academician Expositor of the Baomo Hall, died at eighty-three, and was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 萬里為人剛而褊。

translations.literal: Wanli's character was firm and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli was by nature firm and narrow.

sentences.zh: 孝宗始愛其才，以問周必大，必大無善語，由此不見用。

translations.literal: Xiaozong at first loved his talent and asked Zhou Bida about him; Bida had no good words—thereby he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong at first valued his talent and asked Zhou Bida about him. Bida spoke ill of him, and he was not employed.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄用事，欲網羅四方知名士相羽翼，嘗築南園，屬萬里為之記，許以掖垣。

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou held power he wished to gather famous men from all directions as wings, once built the Southern Garden, and asked Wanli to write its record, promising him the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou held power he wished to gather famous men as supporters, built the Southern Garden, and asked Wanli to write its record, promising him a Secretariat post.

sentences.zh: 萬里曰：「官可棄，記不可作也。」

translations.literal: Wanli said: "Office may be abandoned; the record cannot be written."
translations.idiomatic: Wanli said, "Office may be abandoned, but the record cannot be written."

sentences.zh: 侂胄恚，改命他人。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was enraged and changed the commission to another.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was enraged and gave the commission to another.

sentences.zh: 臥家十五年，皆其柄國之日也。

translations.literal: He lay at home fifteen years—all days when Tuozhou held power.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at home fifteen years—all while Tuozhou held power.

sentences.zh: 侂胄專僭日益甚，萬里憂憤，怏怏成疾。

translations.literal: Tuozhou's usurpation grew daily worse; Wanli grieved and fretted himself into illness.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou's usurpation grew worse daily; Wanli grieved and fretted himself into illness.

sentences.zh: 家人知其憂國也，凡邸吏之報時政者皆不以告。

translations.literal: His family knew he grieved for the state and did not tell him what courier reports brought of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: His family knew he grieved for the state and withheld courier reports on current policy.

sentences.zh: 忽族子自外至，遽言侂胄用兵事。

translations.literal: Suddenly a clansman came from outside and abruptly spoke of Tuozhou's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a clansman arrived from outside and abruptly spoke of Tuozhou's military campaign.

sentences.zh: 萬里慟哭失聲，亟呼紙書曰：「韓侂胄奸臣，專權無上，動兵殘民，謀危社稷，吾頭顱如許，報國無路，惟有孤憤！」

translations.literal: Wanli wailed aloud, hastily called for paper and wrote: "Han Tuozhou is a treacherous minister who monopolizes power without restraint, mobilizes troops and harms the people, and plots against the altars of state. My head is thus—there is no road to repay the state, only solitary indignation!"
translations.idiomatic: Wanli wailed aloud, called for paper, and wrote: "Han Tuozhou is a treacherous minister who monopolizes power, mobilizes troops and harms the people, and plots against the state. My head is thus—I have no road to serve the realm, only solitary indignation!"

sentences.zh: 又書十四言別妻子，筆落而逝。

translations.literal: He also wrote fourteen characters bidding farewell to wife and children; the brush fell and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote fourteen characters bidding farewell to wife and children; the brush fell and he died.

sentences.zh: 萬里精於詩，嘗著《易傳》行於世。

translations.literal: Wanli was expert in poetry and once wrote Exegesis of the Changes, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli was expert in poetry and wrote an Exegesis of the Changes that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 光宗嘗為書「誠齋」二字，學者稱誠齋先生，賜諡文節。

translations.literal: Guangzong once wrote for him the two characters Sincerity Studio; scholars called him Master Sincerity Studio, and he was granted the posthumous title Wenhjie.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong once wrote for him the two characters "Sincerity Studio." Scholars called him Master Sincerity Studio, and he was granted the posthumous title Wenhjie.

sentences.zh: 子長孺。

translations.literal: His son was Changru.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Changru.
